The proposed framework offers a scalable approach for analysing cyber risks in maritime transport systems and supports risk-informed cybersecurity management.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Travel time models incorporating zone boundaries in SBS/RSs with multiple shuttle carriers
Authors: Jingjing Yang, Ran Chen, Hu Yu
Abstract: Shuttle-based Storage and Retrieval Systems equipped with shuttle carriers (SBS/RS-SC) are an emerging alternative to traditional shuttle-based storage and retrieval systems. In SBS/RS-SC, storage racks are partitioned into multiple zones, each comprising several tiers and served by a dedicated shuttle carrier. Unlike conventional shuttles, these carriers can move horizontally and vertically simultaneously, enabling more efficient load transport within each zone. To evaluate the performance of this system, this paper develops closed-form travel time models for both single-command (SC) and dual-command (DC) operating modes. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the developed models approximate the discrete system with high accuracy, with deviations of less than 3.51%. Building on these validated models, a zone boundary optimization model is further proposed to determine the optimal rack partitioning that minimizes expected travel time. The optimization results show that the performance gap between optimal zoning and equal-sized zoning is less than 4.07% for the SC mode and 0.087% for the DC mode, indicating that simplified equal-sized zoning can provide near-optimal performance in practice. Furthermore, sensitivity analysis reveals diminishing returns to improvements in equipment speed, identifies a practical range for the shuttle speed ratio, and shows that the optimal rack layout depends strongly on the interaction between system kinematics and the shape factor. Finally, the framework is extended to incorporate system throughput, investment cost, class-based storage, and alternative dwell-point policies, thereby providing comprehensive decision support for SBS/RS-SC design and operation.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Dynamic resource allocation for managing homeless shelter requests: An approximate dynamic programming approach
Authors: Sina Ansari, Masih Fadaki, Mohammad Delasay
Abstract: Homeless shelters routinely face the challenge of allocating scarce resources to an unpredictable and diverse population with varying levels of need. This paper develops a dynamic, priority-aligned allocation policy for emergency shelter services, modeled as a finite-horizon Markov Decision Process (MDP). We propose an Approximate Dynamic Programming (ADP) approach that incorporates heterogeneous client classes, stochastic arrivals, and capacity constraints, with service performance weighted by policy-driven priority factors. To facilitate implementation, we translate the optimal policy into practical protection-level rules that reserve capacity for higher-priority classes. Using data from the Australian Specialist Homelessness Services Collection, we present a proof-of-concept numerical study with stylized yet data-informed parameter settings that illustrate how the proposed framework can substantially improve performance over benchmark allocation policies, achieving a fill rate of over 95% for high-priority clients, particularly under resource scarcity. The proposed approach offers a practical and interpretable decision-support tool that enables shelter providers to effectively balance priority-based equity and efficiency.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: A decomposition approach for holistic vessel traffic service planning in seaport waters
Authors: Baoli Liu, Yan Huang, De-Ping Yu, Xiaotian Zhuang, Zhongshuai Wang
Abstract: Efficient management of vessel traffic in seaports depends on three closely linked decisions: vessel sequencing, pilot assignment, and tugboat allocation. Traditionally, these decisions are addressed sequentially, resulting in suboptimal or even infeasible vessel traffic service plans. In this study, we consider a joint vessel sequencing, pilot assignment, and tugboat allocation problem (VSPTAP), in which a seaport manages a diverse team of pilots and a heterogeneous fleet of tugboats to service inbound and outbound vessels. We propose a mixed-integer linear programming model for the VSPTAP, which captures the multi-segment navigation structure, channel restrictions, diverse pilotage and tugboat requirements, and the interactions among the three decision layers, with the objective of minimizing the total delay cost of all vessels. While general-purpose solvers suffice for small-scale instances, we propose a decomposition approach to efficiently handle larger and more practical scenarios. The approach partitions the VSPTAP into a master vessel sequencing problem, together with two subproblems for pilot assignment and tugboat allocation, solved via reinforcement learning, column generation, and column enumeration, respectively. These methods are integrated within a hybrid optimization framework that dynamically coordinates vessel sequencing with pilotage and tugboat schedules. Extensive computational experiments based on Qinzhou Port, China, show that the proposed approach substantially outperforms the benchmark methods from the literature and current practices, yielding satisfactory solutions within 15 minutes and enabling daily cost savings of about RMB 232 thousand for the seaport. Furthermore, managerial insights are offered to support the operations and management of seaport traffic.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Behavioral influences in hedging decisions for commodity purchasing
Authors: Maryam Teymoury, Behnam Fahimnia, Andrew Collins
Abstract: Hedging in commodity purchasing involves securing commodity prices or quantities in advance to protect against price fluctuations and reduce financial risk. This paper examines the impact of risk-taking attitude, confidence level, and numeracy skills on a supply manager’s hedging decisions in commodity purchasing. We employ a discrete choice experiment to test four hypotheses grounded in existing literature. The experiment was designed through extensive consultations with industry practitioners and refined through a pilot study. Using data collected from 136 sourcing managers in the fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) industry, we find that the hedging decisions are significantly influenced by a combination of risk-taking attitude, confidence, and numeracy skills. Risk-taking and confidence are positively associated with riskier hedging choices, while numeracy shows a weaker, negative direct effect, primarily moderated by risk-taking and confidence. These findings deepen our understanding of how specific behavioral traits impact hedging decisions in commodity purchasing, offering practical insights for firms to better align managerial risk preferences with organizational risk management strategies, particularly in volatile market environments.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Trade-offs of recycling strategies under carbon tax and recycling target responsibility system: Trade-in vs. deposit-refund
Authors: Junwei Zhao, Huiqin Zhang, Yexia Zhang, Heli Zhang, Deru Xie, Yuxiang Zhang
Abstract: Under the dual pressures of global climate change and sustainable resource management, carbon taxes and recycling target responsibility systems are synergistically fostering the green transformation of the manufacturing industry through integrated policy combinations. However, optimizing the selection of recycling strategies within reverse logistics under this complex regulatory framework remains a formidable managerial challenge. To explore the operational boundaries of two mainstream recycling strategies, namely Trade-in (TI) and Deposit-refund (DR), we develop a manufacturer-led Stackelberg game model to compare their performance under dual environmental regulations. The findings reveal distinct cost thresholds for strategy selection. TI relies on an internal subsidy mechanism and is particularly effective for products with low production costs and rapid turnover. Its core advantage lies in leveraging discount incentives underpinned by high profit margins to significantly bolster demand for new products. Conversely, DR, which utilizes an external deposit mechanism, yields higher profits in high-cost industries. By externalizing incentive costs, DR maintains a more competitively priced system and effectively steers price-sensitive consumers toward remanufactured products. Interestingly, aligning policy design with the appropriate recycling strategy is key to achieving a triple-win outcome. When production costs are low and carbon taxes are high, TI more effectively balances economic growth, environmental protection, and social welfare. In contrast, DR emerges as the superior choice when production costs are high and carbon taxes are moderate. Our findings provide strategic guidance for firms to optimize recycling choices in reverse logistics and for regulators to orchestrate complementary environmental policies.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Predict-then-optimise interchange control for rail logistics with combined passenger-freight chains
Authors: Elham Ahmadi, André Ludwig, Omid Fatahi Valilai
Abstract: Interchange decisions at rail transfer stations directly affect end-to-end service reliability and cost-to-serve; yet, existing delay-management approaches either forecast delays without prescribing actions or optimise dispatch with coarse delay representations. We propose a predict-then-optimise framework that integrates multi-task LSTM-based delay prediction with a feasibility-constrained Markov Decision Process (MDP) to determine whether to proceed, hold, reschedule, or reroute services at transfer stations. The LSTM models short-horizon delay propagation using only information available at the prediction epoch, while the MDP converts the predicted delay class, capacity regime, infrastructure condition, and bounded dwell feasibility into auditable dispatch recommendations. We evaluate the framework on a three-leg regional rail case study in central Germany comprising lines RB5 (Fulda–Bebra), RB87 (Bebra–Eichenberg), and RB83 (Eichenberg–Kassel), with two physical interchange stations (Bebra and Eichenberg). The results show that the sequence models provide sub-minute ETA accuracy across all three legs and that the Bebra interchange policy reduces the cost-to-serve index by 7.0% relative to the earliest-feasible heuristic while maintaining the same structural miss rate under a 60-minute admissible dwell window. At Eichenberg, the MDP and earliest-feasible policies perform almost identically among evaluable journeys, while the low matched-departure coverage highlights a data and timetable-coordination limitation for full multi-leg evaluation. The framework contributes a deployment-oriented closed-loop architecture in which policy-induced connection gaps are propagated into downstream ETA estimation, supported by per-timestep station embeddings, two-stage cross-leg fine-tuning, and replay-buffer stabilisation. The paper demonstrates how established prediction and control components can be operationally coupled to provide interpretable, manager-facing rail logistics decision support with journey-level KPIs and cost-to-serve reporting.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Vehicle-road-cloud integration: Revolutionizing urban mobility through intelligent transportation systems and advanced traffic flow optimization
Authors: Nok KO, Zhiqin Ma, Changyuan Yu
Abstract: The connection of Vehicles, Road infrastructure and the integration of Cloud computing systems (VRCI) has led to a significant shift in urban transport. The review proposes a new VRCI model that improves urban operations by combining artificial intelligence, the Internet of Things (IOT) and modern network technologies. The paper examines how these elements interact within a within a unified smart city structure. The model focuses on four key innovations that support each other: first, the creation of flexible rules that encourage new technologies while protecting public safety; and second, the use of city-wide sensor networks to gain real-time understanding. Urban activities; third, the application of modern training algorithms to improve traffic; and fourth, ensuring that VRCI development is aligned with the larger objectives of a reasonable city to make more efficient use of resources. Together, these improvements provide a solid foundation for a more efficient and lasting future for cities. The paper also highlighted important challenges, such as data security and the need for global standards. Noting the potential of new tools, such as computing and block chains, to enhance system-wide sustainability. By combining these technical, social and political considerations, it is clear that VIRCI is important not only for improving transport, but also as a key factor in helping cities achieve their sustainable and low-carbon future goals. The study is a practical guide for leaders, researchers and governors who are developing a new generation of smart and liveable cities.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Risk mitigation in perishable supply chains: An AI- driven approach for managing meat distribution
Authors: Bahareh Kargar, Majid Baqeri, Hamed Jahani, Srinivas Talluri
Abstract: The meat supply chain (MSC) faces significant challenges due to the perishability of products, leading to substantial economic and environmental costs. Traditional monitoring and logistics methods often fail to provide real-time predictive insights needed to mitigate spoilage risks. In this study, we propose an artificial intelligence (AI) -driven framework integrating fine-tuned vision-language models (VLMs) – specifically NVILA and Qwen Vision Language (Qwen-VL) – with a robust optimization model for improving freshness prediction and logistics management in MSCs. Using the Meat Freshness Image Dataset, we fine-tune VLMs to classify meat into freshness categories and employ these predictions within a distributionally robust optimization (DRO) model to manage storage, transportation, and spoilage decisions under uncertainty. Our framework leverages Wasserstein-based DRO to model uncertainties in freshness, demand, and transportation times, leading to improved cost efficiency, service levels, and supply chain resilience. Numerical experiments demonstrate that our approach reduces worst-case costs and spoilage compared to nominal optimization methods, offering a scalable and effective solution for perishable supply chain management.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Beggar or enrich-thy-neighbor? Impact of platform cross-border acquisition
Authors: Xiaoran Liu, Xuwei Qin, Lusheng Shao, Xiuqing Gong
Abstract: E-commerce platforms have increasingly pursued cross-border acquisitions in recent years, targeting either foreign online platforms or foreign brick-and-mortar retailers. Motivated by this practice, this paper investigates how the choice of acquisition target reshapes global supply chain dynamics. We develop a game-theoretic model that captures the data-driven network effect associated with acquiring foreign platforms and the in-store service investment and resulting showrooming effect from acquiring foreign retailers. Several findings emerge. First, both acquisition strategies are double-edged swords for the upstream manufacturer. Acquiring a foreign retailer raises the manufacturer’s profit but heightens its exposure to tariff increases, whereas acquiring a foreign platform may reduce its profit but mitigates the adverse effects of tariff increases. Second, the two strategies generate contrasting channel spillovers. Acquiring a foreign platform constitutes a “beggar-thy-neighbor” strategy that benefits acquisition-related channels at the expense of non-acquired channels, whereas acquiring a foreign retailer may serve as an “enrich-thy-neighbor” strategy. Third, provided that the acquisition price is appropriate, either strategy can improve social welfare in both the domestic and foreign countries. Finally, although a stronger showrooming effect may seem to favor the foreign platform, it does not necessarily do so. These findings offer managers a framework for evaluating cross-border acquisition targets and provide policymakers with a welfare-based lens for assessing and regulating such acquisitions.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Physics-informed multi-agent deep reinforcement learning for dynamic emergency resource scheduling in marine oil spills
Authors: Jiahui Yang, Zaijin You, Zhuo Sun, Zhe Ji, Fengwu Wang
Abstract: An efficient marine oil spill response is essential for mitigating environmental impacts. However, dynamic ocean conditions and uncertain spill evolution make timely and flexible emergency resource scheduling challenging. This study proposes a physics-informed multi-agent deep reinforcement learning framework for maritime oil spill response. The framework integrates oil evolution processes and environmental dynamics into the decision-making environment, enabling agents to adapt scheduling strategies under changing spill conditions. A multi-objective reward mechanism is developed to balance recovery performance, response time, and resource utilization. Simulation experiments demonstrate that the proposed MADDPG-based method consistently outperforms benchmark approaches across multiple objectives. Furthermore, the framework is validated using a real-world Bohai Sea oil spill scenario, demonstrating its applicability under realistic marine conditions. Multi-seed experiments show stable performance with a low coefficient of variation of 2.7% for the Overall Performance Index, confirming the robustness and reliability of the proposed approach for intelligent oil spill emergency response.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Multi-dimensional constraint-based vertiport location optimization for urban air mobility
Authors: Meng Zhou, Yuanheng Li, Shaorui Zhou, Lingxiao Wu, Fan Wang, Changmin Jiang
Abstract: Urban Air Mobility (UAM) is an emerging transport mode with the potential to relieve pressure on congested ground networks and is expected to see wider application in the coming years. This study develops an electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) vertiport location selection framework for UAM. In practice, vertiport location is governed by both two-dimensional (2D) land-availability constraints, including land-use compatibility and conflicts with roads and building footprints, and three-dimensional (3D) obstacle-clearance constraints that ensure feasible approach and departure corridors in the urban airspace. These constraints are closely linked to outcomes such as the number of vertiports, construction and operating costs, and travel demand coverage. The proposed framework links demand-informed candidate generation, 2D/3D spatial feasibility screening, and multi-objective location optimization in a unified workflow. It captures the trade-off between passenger generalized travel cost and supply-side fiscal cost under a minimum demand-coverage requirement, and evaluates alternative deployment strategies through multi-scenario analysis. A case study in Shenzhen, China, shows how spatial feasibility constraints, demand coverage, aircraft characteristics, clearance requirements and construction schemes jointly shape cost-effectiveness and deployment strategies for vertiport planning in high-density urban environments. The findings provide planning evidence for aligning spatial feasibility screening, cost trade-offs and staged UAM deployment decisions in dense urban areas.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Low-carbon China-Europe multi-corridor container freight network under shipping disruption risks
Authors: Hairui Wei, Tingting Mao, Sang-Jeong Lee
Abstract: With the various regulations and initiatives by international organizations for decarbonization across the international transport sector, stakeholders should move beyond cost-oriented models toward green transport and logistics management. This study focused on the resilient operation and low-carbon transformation of the China–Europe containerized freight network. Within the diversified transport corridors available for China, including traditional shipping routes, the China Railway Express (CRE), and the Arctic Shipping Route (ASR), a network equilibrium model was constructed with a Logit-based path choice model that incorporates carbon emission costs, in-transit inventory costs, and bottleneck congestion effects. The study evaluated shippers’ path choice behavior and equilibrium changes in the overall network under scenarios involving carbon emission costs, different corridor compositions, and disruptions to critical shipping corridors. An entropy-regularized Frank–Wolfe (ERFW) algorithm was developed to solve the model efficiently. The results indicated that the CRE and the ASR have significant low-carbon advantages. Nevertheless, the advantage may be weakened during extreme peak-demand periods due to capacity constraints. The CRE has a significant regulating effect in enhancing network resilience and mitigating the risks of shipping corridor disruptions, particularly short-term disruptions. The ASR and the CRE showed a complementary relationship in their regulatory effects on carbon emissions and disruptions to critical shipping corridors rather than a substitution relationship. These findings provide decision-makers with insights into planning and operational optimization of the China–Europe containerized freight network under carbon emission costs and the disruption scenarios of critical shipping corridors.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Collaborative multi-depot vehicle routing problem with time windows, split delivery, and uncertain demands
Authors: Yong Wang, Mengyuan Gou, Siyu Luo, Lu Zhen, Xiuling Hei
Abstract: With the rapid development of e-commerce and information technology, customers can add, cancel, or restore orders in real time, and an order can contain multiple incompatible types of commodities that need to be split for delivery. The increasingly uncertain and diverse customer demands have driven a shift from single-depot to multi-depot urban logistics networks. By systematically analyzing the various service area configurations in the multi-depot network, this study rigorously demonstrates that multi-depot collaboration can reduce delivery costs for customers requiring split deliveries. Then, a collaborative multi-depot vehicle routing problem with time windows, split delivery, and uncertain demands (CMDVRPTW-SDUD) is proposed and investigated. To reduce the frequency of vehicle route adjustments during service, the working day is divided into consecutive time slices, transforming CMDVRPTW-SDUD into a series of temporally segmented sub-problems. A time-slice-based mathematical model is formulated to minimize the total operating cost and the number of second-echelon vehicles. An improved K -means++ clustering algorithm is integrated with a multi-objective jellyfish search algorithm with genetic operations (MOJS-GO) to solve the model. The MOJS-GO incorporates a population evolution mechanism and a local search operator to balance convergence speed and solution quality adaptively. An uncertain demand response strategy is designed to address the temporal variability of customer requests, while a vehicle resource sharing strategy reallocates idle second-echelon vehicles to improve utilization. The performance of the proposed method is benchmarked against the CPLEX solver, multi-objective particle swarm optimization, multi-objective difference evolution, and non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II. A real-world case from Chongqing City, China, is used to validate the model and algorithm. Comparative analyses across varying uncertain demand response methods, time slice lengths, reserved second-echelon vehicle loading proportions, and algorithm ablation experiments confirm the robustness of the approach. By jointly considering split deliveries due to incompatible items and real-time demand variation, this study offers a practical solution for building cost-efficient, resource-optimized, and flexible multi-depot transport systems in uncertain environments.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: TrajCleaner: An end-to-end framework for systematic cleaning and completing vessel trajectory data
Authors: Huimin Qiang, Wenlong Niu, Xiaodong Peng, Huanhuan Li
Abstract: Reliable vessel trajectory data are fundamental for maritime situational awareness and intelligent port management, yet Automatic Identification System (AIS) records frequently suffer from drift errors, temporal gaps, and fragmented sequences. Existing studies on AIS trajectory cleaning and gap completion remain limited by fragmented workflows, weak integration between detection and completion, and insufficient adaptivity across heterogeneous maritime environments. To address these challenges, this paper proposes TrajCleaner, a systematic end-to-end framework for trajectory anomaly detection, repair, and event-based completion. This framework integrates adaptive multi-feature detection to identify missing or abnormal segments across diverse vessel types and port operational regimes. A multi-factor weighted similarity mechanism enables robust candidate retrieval, while a spatio-temporal joint completion strategy enforces port-specific navigational constraints and performs density-aware temporal allocation to ensure behavioral plausibility. Unlike prior approaches that treat drift correction, gap detection, and interpolation as independent tasks, TrajCleaner provides a unified pipeline from anomaly recognition to event-level trajectory completion. Experiments using AIS data from the port of Los Angeles (LA) demonstrate that TrajCleaner substantially enhances detection accuracy, completion fidelity, and temporal realism compared with state-of-the-art baselines. By generating eventized and behaviorally coherent vessel trajectories, TrajCleaner improves the analytical depth of downstream maritime applications, including vessel behavior profiling, port operational efficiency assessment, and channel and berth planning. These capabilities provide a more reliable data foundation for predictive, adaptive, and decision-support systems in next-generation smart ports, ultimately strengthening maritime safety, operational efficiency, and environmental sustainability.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: A logic-based Benders decomposition algorithm for anchor position allocation problem
Authors: Baoli Liu, Fan Zhang, Di Wu, Xiaotian Zhuang, Zhongshuai Wang
Abstract: An imbalance between the growing demand for vessel access to anchorage areas and the rigid, scarce supply of anchorage capacity has led to persistent “anchoring difficulties” in port waters. In this paper, we consider the anchor position allocation problem (APAP) that arises from anchorage operations and management. The problem is concerned with serving the demand of a set of calling vessels with the available anchor positions at minimum cost, where some vessels may be denied service if allocation is not cost-effective. The APAP extends traditional variants of the bin packing problem by incorporating practical features: anchor position heterogeneity, vessel navigation directions, and traffic flow control. Despite its theoretical significance and wide-ranging practical relevance, the APAP has received little attention in the literature. We formulate this problem as a mixed-integer linear programming model. General-purpose solvers can handle the model in small-scale scenarios. To address the computational intractability of practical-sized problems, we propose a tailored logic-based Benders decomposition (TLBBD) algorithm with problem-specific optimality cuts, complemented by an exact polynomial-time allocation procedure. Through computational experiments based on the operational data from Zhoushan Port, China, we show that the proposed TLBBD significantly outperforms the Gurobi solver and current industry practices for anchor position allocation. In particular, our algorithm obtains optimal solutions for instances with up to 75 vessels and 30 anchor positions in under ten minutes. Extensive experiments are further conducted to derive managerial insights.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Ride-hailing platform operations and blockchain adoption under service quality uncertainty: quality-, quantity-, and risk-sensitive passengers
Authors: Jing Sun, Shifeng Liu, Daqing Gong, Xiaojie Yan
Abstract: Ride-hailing platforms have become a mature mode of transportation, yet service quality on the supply side remains volatile. Passengers display different risk attitudes toward such fluctuations, making joint pricing and service-quality governance decisions nontrivial. This paper studies how the platform should operate and whether to adopt blockchain in the presence of risk-sensitive passengers. Blockchain enables the platform to better identify passengers’ risk types and implement differentiated decisions. We develop a game-theoretic model with network externalities and further capture the sensitivity of both supply-side and demand-side users to service quality. We find that passengers’ relative sensitivities to service quality and driver quantity shape both the ranking of optimal service-quality governance intensity across risk types and the platform’s overall operating strategy. In particular, higher service quality is not always optimal, as higher prices can still be associated with user growth. Moreover, the same sensitivity structure governs how blockchain adoption modifies the platform’s optimal service-quality governance intensity. In addition, blockchain adoption always benefits drivers; when passengers are highly sensitive to service quality, it can generate mutually beneficial outcomes among passengers, drivers, and the platform. We also emphasize the role of government subsidies when passengers’ sensitivity to service quality is moderate, as the platform has no incentive to adopt blockchain in this case. The main insights remain robust when the platform is risk-averse to profit fluctuations. These findings provide implications for both platform and government.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Platform competition and driver multi-homing in ride-hailing markets
Authors: Yaqian Zhou, He Huang, Hai Yang
Abstract: This paper explores platform competition and driver multi-homing in ride-hailing markets. We propose an equilibrium model of a two-platform system with price- and time-sensitive customers and earnings-sensitive drivers. We consider two separate settings: single-homing where drivers work only for the platform that offers higher earnings, and multi-homing where drivers simultaneously work for two competing platforms. Our framework segments the customer market into two groups: loyal customers, who stick with their preferred platforms, and competitive customers, who always choose the platform that yields higher utility. Within this framework, we first examine how two key features of competitive markets—customer loyalty and platform substitutability—can affect equilibrium prices and wages and resulting market outcomes. We find that, ceteris paribus, an increase in customer loyalty makes all stakeholders worse off, while an increase in platform substitutability benefits customers and drivers at the expense of platforms. Building on this, we explore how multi-homing would impact the interests of different stakeholders. A major result in the multi-homing literature on on-demand service platforms is that both customers and drivers are worse off when drivers multi-home. We show that this result largely depends on assuming away the “pooling effect”—matching becomes more efficient when demand and supply increases proportionally—that is prevalent in on-demand service platforms. By incorporating the “pooling effect”, the findings suggest that multi-homing could make both customers and drivers better off in markets with high competition characterized by low customer loyalty and high platform substitutability. Moreover, our results indicate that all stakeholders could be better off when drivers multi-home in markets where drivers are less heterogeneous in their reservation earnings and the degree of competition is moderate.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Integrating minimum cost flow and capacitated location in global supply chains under uncertainty
Authors: Yi Zhang, Hari Nandan Nath, Stefan Nickel
Abstract: Modern supply chain networks face significant challenges in balancing operational efficiency and resilience under diverse real-world uncertainties such as demand fluctuations and disruptions. To address these complexities, this study proposes an Integrated Capacitated Facility Location and Minimum Cost Flow Problem under Multi-Uncertainty (ICLMF-MU). The integrated multi-objective optimization model simultaneously optimizes total cost, service utility, and total risk while accounting for unmet demands and disruptions in supply chain network design. To deal with the NP-hardness of the problem, we propose an enhanced hybrid non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II (NSGA-II). A novel bi-level evaluation strategy couples an exact linear programming (LP) solver to maintain flow balance with a greedy heuristic as a fallback mechanism. Through a three-stage benchmarking process, the algorithm demonstrates strong convergence and consistent performance. A large-scale numerical study (100 nodes) evaluates performance under diverse global trade environments, contrasting cost-sensitive goods against strategic resources prone to export controls. Pareto frontier trade-off analysis identifies a distinct Criticality Premium, confirming that strategic sectors require a substantially greater investment to withstand sanctions compared to commercial scenarios. Furthermore, regret analysis exposes a Robustness Paradox: the min-risk strategy exhibits the highest operational regret and lowest real-world resilience by limiting network scope. In contrast, the max-utility and balanced strategies demonstrate superior robustness. Sensitivity analysis confirms this implicit redundancy provides the structural capacity needed to absorb large demand surges, with the medical strategy demonstrating superior overall resilience under extreme demand. These findings imply that for critical supplies, true robustness is an emergent property of sufficient capacity investment rather than the optimization of theoretical risk indicators alone, offering guidance for designing resilient networks in an unstable global trade landscape.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: The Braess-like paradox in airline network design: Insights from two case studies
Authors: Yueer Zhou, Yahua Zhang, Linbo Li, Kun Wang, Xiaowen Fu
Abstract: Designing airline networks that enhance profitability through higher load factors and improved revenue generation is a challenging task. Although progress has been made, several issues remain unresolved, particularly regarding the adaptability of existing models to large-scale networks and routing inefficiencies caused by network paradoxes such as the Braess paradox. This study proposes a multi-objective framework for hybrid airline network design based on a self-regulated ant colony optimization (SRACO) algorithm. Case studies of Qantas Airways and China Southern Airlines demonstrate the framework’s applicability across different network settings. The results reveal that the occurrence of a Braess-like paradox in the simulation may lead to resource inefficiency during passenger assignment approaches equilibrium, particularly when network routes and frequencies are optimized. Fortunately, this phenomenon can be mitigated by adjusting hub locations. These findings indicate that network performance is constrained by hub location and highlight the importance of the joint optimization of hubs and routes. Moreover, incorporating hub location adjustments during the design process can mitigate the paradox and enhance airline revenue.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Resource-oriented optimization of electric vehicle systems: A data-driven survey on charging infrastructure, scheduling, and fleet management
Authors: Hai Wang, Baoshen Guo, Xiaolei Zhou, Kun Ding, Shuai Wang, Zhiqing Hong, Tian He
Abstract: Driven by growing concerns over air quality and energy security, electric vehicles (EVs) have experienced rapid development and are reshaping global transportation systems and lifestyle patterns. Compared with traditional gasoline-powered vehicles, EVs offer significant advantages, including lower energy consumption, reduced emissions, and lower operating costs. However, several core challenges remain to be addressed: (i) charging station congestion and operational inefficiencies during peak hours, (ii) high charging costs under time-varying electricity pricing schemes, and (iii) conflicts between charging needs and passenger service requirements. To address these challenges, this paper presents a comprehensive review of resource-oriented optimization models and approaches proposed in the literature. The reviewed studies cover the entire life cycle of EV systems, including charging station deployment, charging scheduling strategies, and large-scale fleet management. In addition, we compare successful and challenging real-world EV deployment cases worldwide to highlight the practical necessity of tailoring optimization algorithms to local infrastructure conditions. Moreover, we discuss the broader implications of EV integration across multiple domains, such as human mobility, smart grid infrastructure, and environmental sustainability, and identify key opportunities and directions for future research.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: The location-routing problem for UAV monitoring under time-varying noise constraints
Authors: Yuping Li, Kewei Xiang, Mingjie Li, Xingyu Wang
Abstract: Noise pollution has emerged as a critical bottleneck hindering the sustainable deployment of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) in urban environments. Current research largely treats facility location and noise-aware routing in isolation, failing to capture the interdependence between strategic infrastructure decisions and tactical compliance operations. This paper bridges this gap by introducing the Location-Routing Problem with Time Windows of the UAVs in Noise-Constrained zones (NC-LRPTW), a joint optimization framework designed for urban UAV monitoring networks. The core innovation lies in modeling flight altitude as a discrete endogenous decision variable, enabling the system to autonomously balance the trade-off between energy-intensive high-altitude flights required for noise abatement and time-penalty costs associated with low-altitude hovering. We formulate this problem as a Mixed-Integer Linear Programming model and propose a tailored two-stage hybrid heuristic algorithm for solving large-scale instances. This algorithm integrates Tabu Search for strategic facility siting with Adaptive Large Neighborhood Search, enhanced by a Departure Time Optimization mechanism, for tactical multi-constraint routing. Computational experiments demonstrate competitive performance against Gurobi on small- and medium-scale instances and effective scalability to complex city-level scenarios derived from real-world data. By internalizing environmental externalities into network design, this study provides a practical decision-support tool for governing the urban low-altitude economy.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Digital twins for low-altitude transportation and logistics: A barrier-centric survey of UAV and eVTOL systems
Authors: Yunshi Zhang, Yuhao Wang, Weimin Zhen, Chunlin Wang, Xiaobo Qu
Abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) platforms are increasingly considered for urban air mobility (UAM), last-mile logistics, and emergency-response operations, yet large-scale low-altitude deployment remains limited. Digital twin (DT) technology supports real-time monitoring, prediction, and control, while existing studies provide limited explanation for why some low-altitude DT application domains advance toward deployment more readily than other domains do. This survey interprets application maturity through a barrier-centric framework that combines a four-layer architecture, feedback-loop timing distinctions, and an application taxonomy organized around three recurring constraints: the Fidelity-Latency Paradox, Information-Theoretic Limits, and the artificial intelligence (AI) Verification Challenge. Scenario comparison across urban UAM, rural or peri-urban logistics, and emergency response shows that the same DT architecture can imply different deployment boundaries depending on operational role, feedback timing, and non-technical conditions. Across applications, predictive maintenance and diagnostic functions appear comparatively mature, whereas path planning, traffic management, and safety-critical real-time control remain more constrained by computational, communication, and assurance requirements. For transportation and logistics research, the main implication is that DT deployment should be assessed by how computational limits, communication capacity, and certification requirements interact with regulation, infrastructure, and business conditions.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Balancing competition and collaboration in carbon-regulated supply chains through shared green logistics
Authors: Salman Piri, Bahman Manafi, Hadi Gholizadeh
Abstract: This paper examines how competing firms can balance competition and collaboration in carbon-regulated supply chains through shared green logistics. The study considers an integrated supply chain network involving facility configuration, supplier selection, shared green distribution centers (DCs), inventory positioning, multimodal transportation planning, and dynamic pricing decisions under competitive and cooperative interactions among firms. The proposed framework explicitly integrates logistics infrastructure sharing, transportation mode selection, and carbon-compliance mechanisms to support efficient freight operations across multiple distribution echelons and market channels. A bi-level game-theoretic optimization model is developed in which firms simultaneously determine strategic network configuration, logistics collaboration, carbon-compliance decisions, and channel-specific pricing policies. The upper-level captures strategic interactions through a generalized Nash equilibrium (GNE) framework, whereas the lower level determines firm-level operational decisions under capacity, demand, and emission constraints, including carbon tax and cap-and-trade mechanisms. Building upon this supply chain network design foundation, the model evaluates three strategic interaction regimes. Non-cooperation (NC), full cooperation (COOP), and a novel hybrid competitive–cooperative (HYB) setting in which firms share logistics infrastructure and environmental investments while retaining pricing autonomy in downstream markets. This hybrid coopetitive structure, largely absent from the supply chain network design literature, enables firms to exploit logistics synergies while preserving competitive incentives. To solve the resulting multi-level mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) problem, a master–oracle solution architecture is developed that combines Logic-Based Benders with Equilibrium Oracles (LBB-EO) and Dual-Calibrated Equilibrium Cuts (DCEC). The framework is validated through a real-world consumer electronics supply chain case study that incorporates empirical demand data, carbon-pricing benchmarks, and logistics infrastructure constraints. Results demonstrate that the HYB maximizes profit in typical parity/competition settings by monetizing service gains while exploiting pooled logistics. Furthermore, COOP is most robust when rail is scarce, quotas bind, or parity tightens, achieving the smallest profit drawdowns and deeper abatement at low marginal cost. Sensitivity analyses reveal that service- and carbon-aligned levers (higher service weight, lead-time penalties, rail capacity, and green-DC effectiveness) shift flows from fragmented trucking to consolidated rail via the shared hub, lowering operating costs and emissions with smooth, monotone responses.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Trade-in strategy: the impact of strategic consumers on competitive supply chains
Authors: Tao Jiang, Kaigeng Shen, Youwei Guo, Xingzheng Lu
Abstract: Advancements in data technology enable firms to collect consumer purchase history data on a broader scale. This not only facilitates the recycling of old products (trade-in programs) but also supports the implementation of behavior-based pricing (BBP) using historical data to boost sales of new products. However, this has also intensified competition among firms. This paper constructs a two-period dynamic pricing model to examine the interactive effects of BBP and cross-brand trade-in strategies under different closed-loop supply chain channel structures. The research findings reveal changes in trade-in rebate, product prices, channel member profits, consumer surplus, and social welfare. We find that, first, BBP may either intensify or alleviate competition in trade-in rebate schemes. Second, firms adopting uniform pricing (UP) should implement price increases in the second period, while those adopting BBP should adopt price decreases to counter competition. Third, UP generates greater total supply chain profits, while BBP consistently increases consumer surplus; however, BBP leads to inferior social welfare. Finally, we extended the model in six dimensions. Finally, we extended the model in six dimensions to capture more realistic competitive scenarios and test the robustness of key findings. These extensions include asymmetric channel structures, salvage values of old products, consumer switching costs, discount factors, consumer retention of old products, and market partial coverage. This work provides some theoretical insights for government agencies in developing a competition regulatory framework that balances firm profits and consumer welfare.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Resilient hybrid air-ground networks for disaster preparedness and response: A distributionally robust approach
Authors: Hengxing Zhao, Zijian Zhao, Pengcheng You
Abstract: Disaster relief operations are frequently paralyzed by substantial network failures that sever access to affected regions during the critical “golden period”. While traditional logistics rely on ground transport and strategic airlift, their effectiveness can be compromised by correlated infrastructure collapse or airport bottlenecks. We develop a resilient network design framework that jointly optimizes facility location, inventory pre-positioning, contingent strategic- and tactical-air capacity, and supporting charging investment for tactical air operations. Motivated by the prohibitive ownership costs of such assets, we model the acquisition of tactical capacity (eVTOLs) through contingent contracts, enabling a flexible response. The problem is formulated as a two-stage distributionally robust optimization model with a Wasserstein ambiguity set to hedge against joint uncertainty in demand and road connectivity under limited data. This ambiguity structure preserves empirical joint-scenario information and leads to an exact decomposition scheme based on sample-wise evaluation blocks. Computational experiments on the Yushu earthquake and the U.S. hurricane season show that the preferred portfolio depends strongly on disruption topology. In Yushu, the robust solution shifts toward tactical bypass capability, and the tactical layer acts as a lifeline bridge when road fragmentation blocks access. In the hurricane case, overall portfolio scale changes less, while inventory and airlift are repositioned across the regional network; there the tactical layer plays a supporting redistribution role within a broader air-ground architecture.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Timing the vaccine flow: An intelligent navigator for strategic delivery and coverage
Authors: Mahsa Mohammadi, Mohsen Roytvand Ghiasvand, Babak Mohamadpour Tosarkani
Abstract: The unprecedented impacts of the COVID-19 outbreak have increased global interest in secure and efficient vaccine distribution. This study investigates the challenges of planning vaccine distribution, including demand fluctuations, limited data availability, and inequitable access to vaccines. It focuses on the allocation of vaccines to mobile and stationary Public Health Units (PHUs) and the management of demand through online registration and real-time updates. To address these challenges, we develop a data-driven Decision Support Framework (DSF) comprising a data-based and a model-based framework. The data-based framework introduces an augmented robust optimization approach that uses dynamic uncertainty sets to adapt to changing conditions. Two data generation algorithms, integrated with predictive analytics, enhance limited data, improve out-of-sample performance, and increase the explainability of robust solutions. These uncertainty sets are fed into the model-based framework, which integrates three mathematical models to dynamically configure PHUs and optimize the vaccination distribution plan. As a conceptual contribution, a new policy is proposed to maximize coverage through a Dynamic PHU Allocation (DPA) algorithm that updates mobile PHU locations. Additionally, an assignment model reallocates surplus inventory to address shortages and ensures proper storage for future use. The numerical results demonstrate that the proposed DSF enables adaptive decision-making, effectively coping with fluctuations in vaccination demand and reducing vaccination shortages by 80% compared to other approaches. The adaptability of the DSF, combined with the role of mobile PHUs in managing demand fluctuations and ensuring equitable access, offers insights for resource allocation and logistical planning in uncertain scenarios.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Seismic resilience assessment and multi‑phase optimization method of regional road networks for earthquake rescue
Authors: Yue Su, Xiushi Dong, Hongjun Cui, Minqing Zhu, Xinwei Ma, Weijie Yu
Abstract: High-resilience road networks are critical for improving rescue efficiency and reducing seismic losses. Existing studies have proposed effective seismic resilience assessment and optimization methods for single phases (pre-earthquake, during-earthquake, post-earthquake). However, the improvement mechanism and effectiveness of multi‑phase resilience optimization framework remain understudied, which limits the construction of high‑resilience road networks. In this context, this study proposes a seismic resilience assessment and multi‑phase optimization method of regional road networks for earthquake rescue. Firstly, a multi–state damage model of road networks is developed by considering complex topological connected relations and multi–state damage characteristics of road components. Then, a probabilistic method is proposed for multi-state road network performance evaluation. This performance is quantified via total travel time for rescue demand. After that, a resilience assessment framework encompassing resistance, adaptation, and recovery capacities is established by linking the rescue process to network performance. Based on this framework, a multi–phase resilience optimization model is formulated to maximize expected resilience under seismic uncertainty by integrating pre–earthquake reinforcing, during–earthquake monitoring, and post–earthquake repairing strategies. Finally, the proposed method is demonstrated using a real regional road network and more than 300,000 simulated scenarios. Under consistent cost constraints, the resilience improvement effect of the multi–phase combined optimization strategy is significantly better than any single–phase strategies. Crucially, the resilience improvement of this combined optimization strategy proves robust across diverse uncertain scenarios. This system–level resilience improvement can be explained by complementary and distinct improvement mechanisms associated with each phase. This provides theoretical and methodological support for planning high–resilience road networks and multi–phase resilience optimization strategy.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Vertiport capacity planning and operations for urban air mobility commuting
Authors: Mengxin Qin, Tie-Qiao Tang, Tao Wang, Shangwu Wen, Haijun Huang
Abstract: Urban air commuting (UAC) represents a vital phase in the evolution of low-altitude transportation. Vertiports are the core of urban air commuting, serving as the hubs that connect passengers with aircraft. Their capacity and operational efficiency directly affect service quality. Thus, understanding how vertiports, in terms of both planning and operations, impact the urban air commuting system is essential. To facilitate this understanding, we construct an aggregate model to describe the economic behavior of the UAC service. From the demand perspective, we employ the bottleneck model integrated with a discrete choice framework to characterize commuter behavior and departure time preferences. On the supply side, we adopt a profit maximization model to delineate the operator’s strategic decisions. This includes the optimal planning and allocation of vertiport land resources, ensuring efficient infrastructure utilization. We employ a queuing model with a buffer to characterize the matching process between commuters and flying car units. In this context, the buffer represents a surplus of vehicles staged at the vertiport relative to the number of available boarding gates, thereby ensuring service continuity and operational stability. The results in the analytical solutions and numerical tests reveal that excessive investment costs can deter operator participation due to sub-optimal returns. To improve system performance, we evaluate the effectiveness of various policy instruments-such as subsidies, maximum price limits, and service quality standards-in regulating and supporting the burgeoning urban air mobility (UAM).
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Prompt and sequential selection transfer based large language model for traffic prediction with limited data
Authors: Xiaojun Bi, Yuzhan Li, Yiwen Sun, Heng Chang, Ke Cheng, Delong Zhu, Bowen Du
Abstract: In the field of intelligent transportation systems, data scarcity severely constrains the generalization capability and precision of prediction models. Existing transfer learning methods often suffer from negative transfer due to discrepancies between source and target domains, compromising prediction performance. Although current LLMs exhibit strong feature learning capabilities, they primarily depend on pretrained knowledge and make insufficient use of source city data for targeted training. Moreover, they fail to conduct in-depth exploration of the characteristics inherent in limited datasets. To address this issue, we propose a Prompt and Sequential Selection Transfer based Large Language Model (PST-LLM) for traffic prediction with limited data, which represents the first effort to leverage LLMs specifically for traffic prediction under limited data without relying on conventional transfer learning frameworks. First, we develop a Source City Sequential Selection (SCSS) strategy for knowledge fusion. Combined with simulated fine-tuning on data-rich source cities, this approach precisely identifies optimal transfer paths to mitigate negative transfer induced by data scarcity. Second, we incorporate text prompts to enable deep fusion of semantic cues with spatio-temporal data. This integration guides the model to efficiently capture traffic patterns under limited data. Finally, a joint pruning and freezing strategy is adopted to streamline model parameters, suppressing overfitting during limited data training and significantly enhancing generalization capability. Experimental results show that PST-LLM consistently outperforms state-of-the-art(SOTA) across real-world datasets under identical settings. Furthermore, PST-LLM not only can generates predictive outputs but also can produces interpretable reasoning analysis and actionable travel recommendations. This is achieved through a dedicated reasoning branch that decodes the model’s high-level embeddings into natural language based on prompt engineering. The source code for PST-LLM is available at https://github.com/pku-smart-city/source:code/tree/main/PST-LLM .
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Structural resilience assessment of Alliance-Based liner shipping Networks: A Dismantling-Based approach
Authors: Yang Yang, Kaimin Chen, Hao Wang, Kevin X. Li
Abstract: Liner shipping network resilience is crucial in the face of growing complex disruptions. Studies have shown these networks are resilient to random failures, while vulnerable to targeted attacks. Previous targeted attack strategies, which rely on centrality rankings or fixed-set dismantling, tended to overestimate network resilience. To address this, this study proposes a sequence-based framework to assess network resilience. An Optimized Node Sequence (ONS) strategy, which formulates dismantling as a bi-objective trade-off between minimizing attack cost and maximizing attack damage, is proposed and solved via a domain-tailored evolutionary algorithm with hybrid initialization. The framework is empirically validated using a longitudinal analysis of annual Ocean Alliance liner services (2017–2025) and ONS is benchmarked against rank-based and set-based strategies. Results show that ONS consistently outperforms the two baselines, identifying ports that trigger early-stage disruptions. The findings further indicate that network resilience fluctuates in response to both internal design choices and exogenous shocks. Furthermore, the service adjustments implemented by the Ocean Alliance during the Red Sea crisis effectively maintained network resilience at a level comparable to that of the pre-crisis designed service network. The proposed framework advances resilience analysis by shifting from set identification to dynamic sequence optimization, offering a decision-support tool for enhancing network resilience planning.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Marching towards maritime decarbonization: Could self-operated fleets hedge cost and consumer payment uncertainty risks?
Authors: Baozhuang Niu, Enkai Zhang, Fengfeng Xie, Hongzhi Wang
Abstract: Maritime transport is the major source of global carbon emissions. While logistics service providers have made substantial investments in decarbonization initiatives, their volatile shipping fees will significantly influence the demand volume, harming the consignor’s ability to jointly achieve profitability and environmental sustainability goals. Such risks can be further enhanced if consumers have reservations when they pay the bill for both goods and their green mindfulness. Therefore, in this study, we investigate whether the consignor’s self-operated fleets could mitigate the negative impacts of cost uncertainty and consumer green concern risks. Although it becomes the consignor who invests in carbon reduction, we reveal that the mitigated cost uncertainty and double marginalization effect help effectively hedge consumers’ payment hesitation when they have uncertain green mindfulness. We find that the consignor’s preference for building the self-operated fleet exhibits a non-monotonic pattern (shifting from self-operated fleet to logistics service providers and then back) as the initial carbon emission intensity increases. We identify an investment failure zone where aggressive carbon reduction via self-operated fleet suppresses sales quantity, thus reducing the consignor’s profitability. Regarding the system’s sustainability performance, we point out that more carbon reductions might boost demand, and hence, increase overall shipping volume and net emissions. These findings underscore the complexities in balancing logistics autonomy and environmental responsibility, offering useful insights for consignors’ developing overseas business.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Beyond efficiency: societal benefit perception as a driver of public acceptance for UAM-based last-mile delivery in Japan
Authors: Dohyung Kim, Sunbin Yoo, Shunsuke Managi, Zheng Chang
Abstract: This study examines the attitudinal drivers of drone delivery acceptance in Japan using a stated-preference discrete-choice experiment in a nationally distributed Japanese survey of 5,113 respondents (with the ICLV estimates based on the 3,592 drone-aware respondents) and a simultaneous integrated choice and latent variable (ICLV) model incorporating six latent constructs. Three principal findings emerge. First, the baseline drone alternative-specific constant is not statistically distinguishable from zero among drone-aware respondents, consistent with acceptance being shaped primarily by the attitudinal and attribute channels in the model. Second, willingness-to-pay (WTP) for institutional trust and equity attitudes represents sizable monetary valuations when their direct and mediated pathways are combined: TRUST ¥34.5 (of which 19.3% is mediated through Perceived Societal Benefit) and EQUITY ¥30.4 (of which 51.4% is mediated). Third, a two-class latent class analysis identifies two distinct preference segments, a TRUST-Affective segment (50.2% of respondents) responsive to institutional and equity attributes, and a Price-Insensitive/Functional segment (49.8%) responsive primarily to operator identity and delivery lead time. These findings suggest that investments in institutional trust and societal benefit communication may generate acceptance returns comparable to operational improvements, offering guidance for socially sustainable UAM logistics policy.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Strategic disclosure of emissions under supplier competition
Authors: Amirmohsen Golmohammadi, Armaǧan Özbilge, Samuel Yousefi
Abstract: Growing concerns about climate change have prompted governments to require firms to disclose greenhouse gas emissions, including those across supply chains (Scope 3). To estimate supplier emissions, firms may rely on secondary data (e.g., industry averages) or primary data reported by suppliers. When a supplier reports emissions below the industry average, the buying firm can reduce its reported Scope 3 emissions, creating a competitive advantage. We develop a game-theoretic model to study how competition shapes suppliers’ emissions measurement and disclosure decisions in a supply chain with one firm and two competing suppliers. We show that disclosure strategies are governed by two thresholds, responsiveness and disinvestment, that together determine when disclosure is unconditionally optimal, strategically conditional, or never beneficial. Counterintuitively, lower measurement costs, higher industry-average emissions, or greater production capacity can lead suppliers to stop measuring emissions, as competitive dynamics can eliminate the informational advantage disclosure provides. The structural properties of this threshold framework are robust across several extensions, including post-disclosure pricing, delayed disclosure, buyer transparency, and fixed adoption costs. These findings reveal that incentive mechanisms targeting individual suppliers can have unintended consequences for overall disclosure rates, offering actionable guidance for firms seeking to improve Scope 3 reporting transparency.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Bi-objective electric vehicle routing with charging–swapping replenishment and location-dependent waiting time
Authors: Xin Zhang, Jiantong Zhang, Tingting Chen
Abstract: The rapid adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) in logistics distribution has created new fleet-routing challenges related to limited driving range, station congestion, and multiple replenishment options. This paper studies a bi-objective electric vehicle routing problem with location-dependent waiting time (BEVRP-LD), in which partial charging and battery swapping are jointly considered under customer time-window commitments. The problem aims to reduce operational cost while improving customer satisfaction. Waiting time is represented as a location- and technology-dependent delay, estimated using an M / M /1 queue for partial charging and an M / D /1 queue for battery swapping. The model jointly determines vehicle routes, station selection, replenishment technology choice, and charging amount under partial charging, while representing customer satisfaction through soft time windows. A mixed-integer linear programming formulation and a clustering-enhanced NSGA-II-based solution framework are developed to generate cost–service trade-off solutions. Computational experiments on benchmark instances and an urban distribution case associated with JD Logistics in China show that the proposed framework can generate diverse Pareto solutions and make the underlying cost–service trade-off explicit. The results indicate that the hybrid use of charging and swapping can improve the balance between cost and service performance, while location-dependent waiting time changes replenishment technology choice and improves the operational realism of routing decisions. The case-based analysis further provides managerial insights into replenishment strategy selection, the use of location-dependent waiting-time information, and the effects of key economic and operational conditions.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Learning from risk: LLM-guided generation of safety-critical scenarios with prior knowledge
Authors: Yuhang Wang, Heye Huang, Zhenhua Xu, Kailai Sun, Baoshen Guo, Jinhua Zhao
Abstract: Autonomous driving faces critical challenges in rare long-tail events and complex multi-agent interactions, which are scarce in real-world data yet essential for robust safety validation. This paper presents a high-fidelity scenario generation framework that integrates a conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE) with a large language model (LLM). The CVAE encodes historical trajectories and map information from large-scale naturalistic datasets to learn latent traffic structures, enabling the generation of physically consistent base scenarios. Building on this, the LLM acts as an adversarial reasoning engine, parsing unstructured scene descriptions into domain-specific loss functions and dynamically guiding scenario generation across varying risk levels. This knowledge-driven optimization balances realism with controllability, ensuring that generated scenarios remain both plausible and risk-sensitive. Extensive experiments in CARLA and SMARTS demonstrate that our framework substantially increases the coverage of high-risk and long-tail events, improves consistency between simulated and real-world traffic distributions, and exposes autonomous driving systems to interactions that are significantly more challenging than those produced by existing rule- or data-driven methods. These results establish a new pathway for safety validation, enabling principled stress-testing of autonomous systems under rare but consequential events. Code is available at https://github.com/echoleaeperw/LRF .
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: A two-layer approach of integrating trajectory planner and motion controller for connected and automated buses under mixed traffic flow
Authors: Tianqi Wang, Weihan Xu, Xin Li
Abstract: This study proposes a hierarchical framework for the trajectory planning and motion control of connected and automated buses (CABs) operating in mixed traffic environments alongside connected and automated vehicles (CAVs) and human-driven vehicles (HVs). Then, a two-layer optimization model is developed, in which the upper-layer maneuver planner optimizes the spatiotemporal positions of CABs and CAVs under bus routing constraints, while the lower-layer vehicle controller is responsible for trajectory planning and the execution of control commands in connection to the spatiotemporal constraints from the upper layer. To solve this constrained optimal control problem and address environmental uncertainties, a customized algorithm integrating a Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP) with Sequential Quadratic Programming (SQP) is designed. Extensive simulations show that the proposed model and algorithm reduce bus schedule deviation by 77.2%, concurrently increase overall traffic throughput by 30%, and lower average delay by 46.4%. Maximum performance is achieved at 60% CAV penetration, highlighting the framework’s potential for cost-effective deployment and significant improvements in both transit punctuality and mixed-traffic efficiency.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Electric vehicle routing problem with multi-visit drones considering time windows and battery swapping stations
Authors: Shanshan Meng, Hongwei Ma
Abstract: In this study, the conventional vehicle routing problem is extended by introducing an integrated electric vehicle–drone system. Within this framework, electric vehicles stop at customer locations to concurrently deploy multiple drones for making time-constrained deliveries, aiming to minimise the total cost with the inclusion of battery swapping expenditures. In contrast with existing vehicle routing problems involving drones, the proposed approach allows drones to conduct multiple deliveries per trip and incorporates battery swapping stations to support electric vehicle operations. A detailed mixed-integer bilinear programming formulation is developed to enhance the realism of the model. On the basis of an adaptive large neighbourhood search framework, a hybrid metaheuristic algorithm is designed for large instances; this algorithm features tailored removal and repair operators, complementary local search procedures, and a station relocation mechanism. Additionally, preprocessing procedures are integrated to preclude infeasible moves, and an effective algorithm is dedicated to determining electric vehicle waiting times. Various numerical simulations are employed to validate the model, confirm the superior performance and applicability of the proposed approach, and quantify its advantages in terms of optimising waiting times, enabling multiple drone trips and integrating battery swapping stations. A case study further corroborates these findings and provides additional operational and managerial insights into the practical implementation of these strategies. These features highlight the cost advantages of the integrated system over an electric vehicle-only paradigm, achieving an average cost reduction of approximately 30%. Furthermore, compared with benchmark algorithms from the literature, the proposed algorithm improves the quality of the output solutions by more than 10%.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Flexible yard template planning with variable size sub-blocks in container terminals
Authors: Haixia Wu, Junliang He, Caimao Tan, Yu Wang
Abstract: To address the rigidity caused by fixed sub-block capacities in container terminal yards, this study proposes a flexible yard template planning method based on variable size sub-block. In this method, sub-block capacity is modeled as a decision variable, and sub-block boundaries are dynamically adjusted according to route specific container volumes and vessel operation time windows, enabling flexible space allocation. Based on this approach, a mixed-integer programming model is developed to jointly optimize sub-block partitioning and allocation, with the objective of minimizing operational costs while maximizing yard space utilization. To efficiently solve the model, an improved Benders decomposition algorithm is designed, incorporating heuristic initial solutions and Pareto-optimal cuts. Numerical results show that, compared with fixed size strategies, the proposed method can reduce yard bay requirements by approximately 16% to 21.7% across different problem scales. Sensitivity analysis further indicates that vessel operation time is a key factor affecting optimal sub-block sizing, and that a nonlinear trade-off exists between transportation costs and delay penalty costs.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: The integrated time slot pricing and on-demand food delivery routing problem with demand and travel time uncertainty
Authors: Yuchen Zhang, Runliang Dou, Meng Zhao, Peng Sun
Abstract: In this paper, we address the integrated problem of differentiated time slot pricing (DTSP) and order dispatching for on-demand food delivery platforms, with a focus on managing both demand and travel time uncertainty and complex operational constraints. A robust two-stage stochastic programming model is proposed. In the first stage, delivery fees for different time slots are selected and combined with a dynamic pricing mechanism that accounts for delivery distance and order value. In the second stage, a budget uncertainty set enables the multi-wave pickup and delivery plan to explicitly withstand fluctuations in trip duration while integrating factors such as restaurant preparation time, rider waiting time, and vehicle load capacity. To solve large-scale instances efficiently, we develop a Robust Adaptive Large Neighborhood Search (RALNS) algorithm enhanced with tailored operators and a hybrid dispatching engine. This engine combines heuristic order bundling with a compact set-partitioning mixed-integer linear program to ensure optimal assignment. Extensive computational experiments using the Meituan TSL Challenge dataset demonstrate that the proposed hybrid approach achieves an average optimality gap of less than 1% for small-scale instances while maintaining computation efficiency for larger-scale instances. Sensitivity analysis indicates that the robust framework increases realized profit by 5% to 15% over deterministic approaches by significantly reducing delay penalties. Furthermore, the dynamic pricing scheme achieves approximately 20% higher overall profitability compared to fixed pricing strategies.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Robust heterogeneous bus-assisted drone delivery under transit uncertainty and drone failures
Authors: Xuefeng Jin, Mingyang Pei, Lingshu Zhong
Abstract: Bus-assisted drone delivery can extend drone service range by using existing public transit resources, but its practical deployment is challenged by heterogeneous drone capabilities, customer time windows, bus transit uncertainty, and drone failure risk. This paper studies the Heterogeneous Bus-Assisted Drone Delivery Routing Problem with Time Windows and Drone Failures and incorporates a robust optimization framework to handle bus transit uncertainty. A mixed-integer nonlinear programming model is developed to minimize the worst-case total cost, including fixed dispatch cost, working time cost, and expected loss of demand (ELOD). Bus transit uncertainty is described by a polyhedral uncertainty set, while drone failure risk is quantified through a Weibull-based failure probability model. To solve the problem efficiently, a JOIH-ALNSLS algorithm is designed by combining a joint optimization insertion heuristic, adaptive large neighborhood search, and variable neighborhood descent local search. Computational experiments show that the proposed algorithm outperforms Gurobi and benchmark metaheuristics. Out-of-sample simulations further demonstrate that robust planning reduces time-window violation risk, and incorporating ELOD lowers both failure risk and actual total cost.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Heterogeneous drone-truck routing problem with En-route operations
Authors: Shuhong Liu, Shaoxuan Zhu, Canrong Zhang
Abstract: The rapid expansion of e-commerce and the increasing complexity of urban logistics have placed unprecedented pressure on last-mile delivery systems. While the integration of drones and trucks offers a promising solution, most existing research restricts drone launch and recovery to fixed customer locations and overlooks the operational flexibility afforded by drone heterogeneity and the multi-visit characteristic. This paper introduces the Heterogeneous Drone-Truck Routing Problem with En-route Launch and Recovery (HDTRP-ELR), which allows multiple heterogeneous drones to launch from and land on a moving truck while performing multi-visit sorties. We formulate a Mixed-Integer Second-Order Cone Programming (MISOCP) model with a payload-dependent energy consumption function. To solve this computationally challenging problem, we propose a Reinforcement Learning-guided Decoupled Adaptive Large Neighborhood Search (RLD-ALNS) algorithm, in which a Deep Q-Network (DQN) agent dynamically selects destruction operators based on the structural features of the current solution. Numerical experiments demonstrate that RLD-ALNS outperforms heuristic baselines by up to 18.0%. The HDTRP-ELR model yields substantial gains over traditional node-restricted models, with en-route launch and recovery alone reducing makespan by 18.5% to 36.5%, and multi-visit capability yielding an additional 8.8% to 13.9%. A heterogeneous drone fleet cuts energy consumption by 23% to 28% versus a homogeneous heavy-duty fleet while preserving makespan. These results demonstrate that the combination of en-route operations, multi-visit sorties, and fleet heterogeneity is key to maximizing the efficiency of next-generation autonomous logistics ecosystems.
