Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Routing coordination optimization for modular electric vehicles in intensive passenger flow evacuation
Authors: Jiarui Yu, Ximing Chang, Qingyun Tian, Huijun Sun, Jianjun Wu
Abstract: For intensive travel demand at transport hubs, commercial districts, or large-scale activity venues, public transportation requires frequent transfers due to fixed stations, routes, and timetables, leading to increased travel uncertainty and time cost. While ride-hailing services offer greater flexibility, the concentration of vehicles exacerbates road congestion and reduces overall transport efficiency. The emerging Modular Electric Vehicles (MEVs) present a promising solution, as they can couple and decouple dynamically along their routes in response to spatiotemporal demand variations and provide door-to-door delivery service. This paper proposes a route collaborative optimization strategy for the efficient evacuation of intensive passenger flows with MEVs, aiming to minimize distance cost while enhancing service efficiency. An integrated clustering-based optimization algorithm (IntCO) is designed to seamlessly integrate demand point clustering and decision-making through policy gradient. Unlike traditional methods, IntCO dynamically adjusts clustering to iteratively refine decision-making, ensuring better alignment with optimization objectives. Real-world case studies demonstrate that MEVs can increase occupancy by 16.2% compared to fixed-capacity shuttle buses and reduce travel distance by 37.7% compared to ride-hailing services. By enabling rapid evacuation of high passenger volumes while providing door-to-door service, MEVs show significant potential for enhancing transportation efficiency and delivering personalized mobility service.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Behaviorally informed optimization of mobility-as-a-service bundle and fleet design for car users
Authors: Si Zhang, Niloufar Javanbakht, Khoa D. Vo, Prateek Bansal
Abstract: Mobility-as-a-Service (MaaS) is widely regarded as a promising strategy for reducing private car dependence. However, existing system-design studies typically rely on simplified or exogenous demand assumptions and often treat fixed-route public transit as the backbone, limiting their ability to capture the behavior of private car users. This is a critical gap, as car users who constitute the primary target for mode shift exhibit strong preferences for door-to-door convenience, reliability, and flexibility that traditional transit systems often cannot satisfy. To address this limitation, we study a demand-responsive multimodal MaaS system centered on shared micro-transit (MoDS) and ride-hailing (RH), two service types capable of replicating key attributes of private car use. We develop a behaviorally grounded optimization framework that jointly determines fleet configuration, service provision, and bundle pricing while endogenizing user subscription and modal choices. On the demand side, we estimate a discrete choice model using stated-preference data from private car owners in Singapore, capturing heterogeneity in sensitivities to travel time, cost, modal composition, waiting, and transfer inconvenience. On the supply side, we formulate a mixed-integer nonlinear program that maximizes a weighted objective combining operator profit and consumer surplus under operational constraints. To ensure computational tractability, we propose an iterative supply-demand optimization method in which supply decisions are updated iteratively with demand responses. We demonstrate the framework through city-scale simulations for 1.2 million car users in Singapore. The results show that up to 43.8% of car trips can be shifted to MaaS and that each MoDS vehicle can replace approximately 2.64 private cars in trip-equivalent terms. These findings highlight the importance of explicitly modeling behavioral responses in MaaS system design and suggest that demand-responsive, car-oriented service configurations can play a central role in reducing private vehicle dependence.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Truck-drone collaborative routing optimization: a unified framework and systematic review
Authors: Yansheng Chen, Jieling Jin, Helai Huang, Wei Liu, Said M. Easa, Yuanwen Lai, Shuyi Wang, Ye Li
Abstract: The collaborative operation of trucks and drones has increasingly emerged as an area of focus in both academic research and industrial applications, driven by the potential to revolutionize logistics and other sectors. This review presents a comprehensive and structured framework designed to systematically categorize and synthesize the existing body of research based on a review of 185 papers published between 2015 and 2025. It encompasses application domains, operational models, fundamental models, solution algorithms, current challenges, and future research directions relevant to truck-drone collaborative operations. The applications of truck-drone collaboration across various sectors are first explored, including logistics, emergency response, and monitoring systems. Three primary operational models of truck-drone collaboration are then analyzed, namely, single-truck and single-drone mode (STSD), single-truck and multiple-drone mode (STMD), and multiple-truck and multiple-drone mode (MTMD). Subsequently, this review classifies the existing mathematical models. It discusses collaboration mechanisms, optimization objectives, constraints, and uncertainty modeling, accompanied by a thorough examination of exact algorithms, approximation algorithms, heuristic algorithms, metaheuristic algorithms, artificial intelligence algorithms, and hybrid algorithms. Finally, the challenges and potential issues encountered in the truck-drone collaboration are summarized, and future research directions are proposed. This review proposes a unified framework for systematically classifying and integrating existing research on truck-drone collaborative routing optimization.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Rolling-horizon UAV dispatch for urban traffic incidents with preparedness-aware repositioning
Authors: Linghui Han, Yue Wu, Chengjuan Zhu, Huijun Sun
Abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) enable rapid aerial response for urban traffic incidents, yet existing work rarely integrates real-time dispatch with anticipatory positioning in an operationally tractable decision model. This study develops a preparedness-aware single-window UAV dispatch model embedded in a rolling decision process. At each scheduling window, the model optimizes current incident response while incorporating a one-step-ahead preparedness term based on predicted regional demand and expected UAV availability in the next window. A mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model jointly optimizes (i) response time and deadline-tardiness penalties in the current window, (ii) next-window preparedness shortfall, and (iii) diversion penalties associated with en-route retasking of returning UAVs and return-depot rebasing penalties. The model captures heterogeneous UAV availability (standby, mission-completed, returning), cross-window state transitions, endurance and service-time constraints, and depot operations. To satisfy online timeliness, we design a two-stage adaptive algorithm: adaptive large neighborhood search (ALNS) produces a dispatch plan, and a MILP repositions idle/returning UAVs; the two stages are coupled via adaptive resource-usage penalty parameters to provide interpretable trade-offs. The method delivers high-quality feasible solutions within minutes. It matches Gurobi’s best feasible solutions on small and medium instances. On large instances, it improves time-limited Gurobi solutions by up to 2.91% and reduces runtime by about one order of magnitude. Sensitivity analyses reveal diminishing marginal returns from fleet expansion and overly conservative repositioning when preparedness is over-weighted, offering guidance for risk-preference calibration and dynamic resource allocation.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: An ∊-logic-based Benders decomposition algorithm for the bi-objective weekly home health care scheduling problem with patient satisfaction
Authors: Juan Du, Yue Xu, Peng Zhu, Xiuli Wang
Abstract: This paper addresses a bi-objective weekly home health care scheduling problem that incorporates patient satisfaction with respect to their preferred service patterns, where a service pattern is defined as a combination of service days and time slot for multiple visits within a week. The objectives are to maximize the number of patients assigned to their preferred patterns and minimize operational costs. In order to provide the trade-offs between the two objectives for decision-makers, we propose an exact ∊-logic-based Benders decomposition (∊-LBBD) algorithm, which embeds the LBBD algorithm in an ∊-constraint framework to generate the Pareto front. In the algorithm, we construct a dynamic cut pool and propose its reuse mechanism to inherit Benders cuts from previously solved ∊-problems exploiting the ascending ∊-iteration framework. For solving each ∊-problem, we introduce the service-pattern conflict inequality into the master problem, and develop a dynamic programming algorithm to solve the resulting subproblems. Computational experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed ∊-LBBD algorithm. By conducting sensitivity analysis on enterprise data, we derive some managerial insights: i) Lowering operational costs comes at the expense of patient satisfaction, and the marginal benefit of cost savings diminishes as satisfaction declines. ii) For a given level of patient satisfaction with preferred patterns, operational costs can be substantially reduced by encouraging patients to specify multiple acceptable service patterns. iii) In response to patients’ service needs, enhancing nurse-patient compatibility through measures such as targeted training can significantly reduce operational costs and/or improve the fulfillment of patients’ preferred service patterns.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Enhancing port channel logistics safety: An asynchronous distributed DRL approach for waterborne ASVs trajectory tracking under dynamic disturbances
Authors: Chongwei Gong, Zhen Tian, Yusheng Zhou
Abstract: Port channel safety is essential for reliable vessel movements and efficient logistics operations in intelligent ports. Waterborne ASVs can support inspection, monitoring, and auxiliary transportation in restricted port waters, but their deployment requires accurate trajectory tracking to avoid additional port-channel navigational safety risks. However, reliable ASV tracking remains challenging under dynamic disturbances and strict ship-to-shore communication constraints. This study proposes an Asynchronous Distributed Deep Reinforcement Learning (AD-DRL) control scheme for robust ASV trajectory tracking under dynamic marine disturbances. Unlike traditional centralized training, the proposed framework enables distributed ASVs to collaboratively update policies by exchanging model gradients rather than raw sensor data, thereby reducing communication requirements. To improve decision-making in dynamic waters, a gated hybrid attention mechanism is integrated into the Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) architecture. This mechanism helps the agent capture spatiotemporal disturbance features and delayed vessel responses caused by hydrodynamic lag. Moreover, an ERA5-informed data-driven simulation environment is constructed using real-world ocean current, wind, and wave data to train and evaluate the controller. Experiments across five representative international ports show that the proposed method achieves lower tracking errors and higher success rates than baseline methods under varying environmental disturbances. Additional safety-corridor analysis further confirms its ability to maintain reliable trajectory execution in port channels. These results demonstrate the robustness and practical relevance of AD-DRL, providing technical support for safer and more reliable ASV operations in intelligent port logistics scenarios.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: A claim cost assessment method of lifetime warranty products with limited usage rate
Authors: Jingqi Liu, Keyao Zhao, Yan Meng, Deyin Jiang, Huan Pang
Abstract: This paper develops a general theoretical framework for claim cost assessment of the lifetime warranty with limited usage rate (LUR-lifetime warranty) in the automotive transportation sector. Firstly, to address limitations in describing consumer heterogeneity, we develop a two-layer nested probability description method that analyzes vehicle usage rates at the overall, group, and individual levels. Secondly, we study the evolution of the usage rate distribution for in-warranty vehicles and propose a warranty rate calculation method. Furthermore, a claim cost assessment model for products with two-dimensional degradation characteristics is established. Finally, the framework reveals the following theoretical properties, illustrated by a case study: (1) usage rate distribution of in-warranty vehicles gradually shifts toward lower usage rates over driving time; (2) instantaneous warranty rate decreases during the first 12 time periods, then increases thereafter; (3) total claim cost per unit increases with higher annual mileage limits under the same driving time, for a 30,000 km limit, the cost after 60 months is about 64% lower than a pure lifetime warranty. The proposed theoretical framework enriches warranty strategy design theory and provides a general analytical tool for vehicle manufacturers and transportation operators.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: A two-stage stochastic programming approach for the time-dependent vehicle routing problem with stochastic demands: a dynamic space–time network perspective
Authors: Chenhao Zhang, Lin Xie, Yaoxin Wu, Tao Feng, Lin Cheng
Abstract: Urban delivery operations increasingly face dual uncertainties from stochastic customer demands and time-dependent traffic, challenging the adequacy of classical vehicle routing models. This study addresses the Time-Dependent Vehicle Routing Problem with Stochastic Demands (TD-VRPSD) with service time windows by constructing a dynamic space–time network aligned with real-world road topology. A two-stage stochastic programming model is developed, integrating preventive and reactive recourse strategies to handle capacity violations under uncertain demands, while explicitly accounting for time-dependent travel times in both routing and round-trip recourse operations, along with service time windows, vehicle waiting and service times. We solve the problem using an improved integer L-shaped method that separates expected-demand routing from scenario-specific recourse and embeds Benders cuts directly into branch-and-bound, dynamically generating cuts during branching. Computational experiments on benchmark instances and a real-world JD.com case show that the proposed method yields adaptive, cost-effective routes, with an average optimal gap of 2.98%, reducing runtime by 39.0%-88.9% while narrowing the optimality gap by 34.1%-84.8% compared to commercial solvers and classical decomposition techniques. Sensitivity analyses on problem scale, demand distribution, deteriorated traffic conditions, and time windows are further conducted, providing relevant managerial insights. This work represents a first attempt to integrate space–time modeling, stochastic demand, hybrid spatiotemporal recourse, and exact decomposition in the TD-VRPSD, providing a framework that can support robust and scalable solutions for urban logistics under uncertainty.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: From regulation to valuation: Carbon pricing signals and eco-technology diffusion
Authors: Hyun-Jung Nam, Doojin Ryu
Abstract: Using monthly data for major tanker and dry bulk segments from 2018 to 2025, we examine whether carbon-pricing signals, measured by European Union Allowance (EUA) prices, are associated with eco-vessel diffusion, measured by eco-vessel share and eco-vessel price premiums. We find that stronger carbon-pricing signals are associated with increases in both dimensions of eco-vessel diffusion. A USD 1 increase in the EUA price is associated with a 0.02 percentage point increase in eco-vessel share over horizons ranging from three to twenty-four months. Over the twelve- to twenty-four-month horizon, the same increase raises eco-vessel price premiums by approximately USD 40,000–60,000.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Joint optimization of fleet size and operating speed for service planning in oversaturated urban rail transit networks
Authors: Siyu Zhuo, Xiaoning Zhu, Pan Shang, Zhengke Liu, Feixiong Liao
Abstract: Oversaturated operations have become increasingly common in urban rail transit (URT) systems, where peak-period passenger demand often exceeds available service capacity. This demand–capacity imbalance leads to platform queues, in-train crowding, and denied boarding, making service planning particularly challenging when fleet resources are limited. To address the coupled supply–demand interactions, this study proposes a novel Behavior–Energy-Adaptive Service planning (BEAS) framework for network-wide URT service planning, in which fleet allocation and line-level operating speed are jointly optimized while passengers’ adaptive route choices are explicitly modeled. An integrated nonlinear integer programming model is developed to link fleet–speed service-plan decisions, subject to fleet budget limits and speed-dependent traction energy costs, with passenger assignment and path-size logit (PSL)-based route choice in a capacity-constrained space–time network. By enforcing train capacity and first-in-first-out (FIFO) boarding, the model reproduces platform queueing and denied boarding, and captures how the resulting time-dependent travel costs drive adaptive rerouting under oversaturated conditions. To solve the resulting large-scale coupled problem, a decomposition-based iterative algorithm is developed, in which the demand-side subproblem simulates individual passenger assignment under time-dependent costs and the supply-side subproblem optimizes fleet and speed decisions through an incremental approximation that yields a tractable multiple-choice knapsack structure. Numerical experiments on both a small illustrative network and a large-scale Beijing metro network demonstrate the computational efficiency, scalability, and practical value of the proposed framework. The results show that coordinated fleet–speed service planning can substantially reduce waiting time and left-behind passengers under resource constraints, while supporting passenger-oriented, operator-oriented, and balanced service planning.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Vessel traffic flow prediction for smart port logistics: A hierarchical adaptive spatio-temporal transformer
Authors: Haowen Lei, Jiajing Chen, Haijiang Li, Shuai Jia, Xinjian Wang
Abstract: Reliable vessel traffic flow (VTF) prediction is essential for proactive port management and maritime safety. However, current VTF prediction paradigms are hindered by four critical challenges: (1) heterogeneity among the retained prediction inputs, including vessel counts, spatial descriptors, and temporal indicators; (2) multi-scale noise in non-stationary temporal dynamics; (3) rapid topological shifts in port networks; and (4) temporal observation sparsity impacting long-horizon prediction robustness. To address these limitations, we propose a Hierarchical Adaptive Spatio-Temporal Transformer (HAST-Former). The approach integrates four specialized modules: (1) a Data Embedding Layer (DEL) to align vessel counts, spatial descriptors, and temporal indicators into a common latent space; (2) a Multi-Scale Temporal Guidance (MSTG) module to suppress recording noise while capturing hierarchical temporal patterns; (3) an Adaptive Spatial Graph Convolution (ASGC) module to reconstruct port topologies based on real-time traffic states; and (4) a Spatio-Temporal Self-Attention (STSA) mechanism with partitioned heads and relative temporal biases (ALiBi) to ensure stable long-horizon prediction under sparse and noisy observed conditions. Extensive evaluations on large-scale datasets from Shanghai and Zhoushan ports demonstrate that HAST-Former consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. These results demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method and highlight its potential for smart port logistics applications.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: A practical approach to multi-day dynamic pricing in attended home delivery
Authors: Hsin Kai Huang, Ryota Okazaki, Yuki Oyama
Abstract: This paper proposes a sampling-based dynamic pricing approach for attended home delivery (AHD), utilizing approximation methods to improve both calculation efficiency and profitability. First, the pricing mechanism is formulated as a choice-based optimization to reflect individual customer preferences. To account for the sequential arrival of multiple customers, the problem is extended to a Markov decision process (MDP) framework. For practical use, a logistics platform must determine prices within 100 milliseconds to ensure a seamless experience for each customer. However, the computational complexity of vehicle routing combined with future uncertainty regarding multi-day customer choices leads to the curse of dimensionality, making real-time application computationally infeasible. To address these challenges, we introduce area-based (Continuous Approximation and Regression-based) and route-based (Cheapest Insertion) approximation methods. Crucially, a sampling-based approximation is developed to mitigate future uncertainty across multi-day delivery options, thereby overcoming the computational barriers of the MDP framework. The performance of each method is evaluated via simulation, incorporating a nested logit model estimated from large-scale stated choice data to reflect realistic delivery timing preferences. The results show that dynamic pricing outperforms fixed pricing, with all methods meeting the required speed limitations (100 milliseconds). After integrating the sampling-based model, profits increase across all approximation methods. Additionally, we evaluate the model under different cost-scaling factors, slot capacities, and customer preferences. The results show that sampling-based policies generally improve profit, with route-based approximation maintaining the highest average profit across the tested settings. This efficient approach provides a scalable and robust solution for dynamic time slot pricing in real-world logistics platforms.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Modeling a resilient port industry and logistics system under global geopolitical and economic uncertainties
Authors: Zhongbin Zhao, Zhenhang Zhou, Jihong Chen, Mengru Shen, Hao Wang, Kee-hung Lai, Chuan Pang, Dairong Wang
Abstract: Global geopolitical conflicts, macroeconomic volatility, and decarbonization compliance pressures are profoundly reshaping the operational logic of the port industry and logistics system. Existing studies focus on natural disaster defense or short-term operational recovery, lacking a forward-looking investment planning framework that integrates geopolitical scenarios, port-centric industry clusters, and transshipment carbon reduction. A significant gap remains in modeling the dynamic interplay among structural risks, industrial layout, and capital allocation. To address this challenge, this paper constructs a multi-stage stochastic programming model encompassing five dimensions, including port operations, direct and indirect supporting industry clusters, low-carbon transshipment, and disruption prevention-recovery. This model simulates four geopolitical scenarios ranging from normal status to extreme conflict. It employs a two-stage adaptive decision architecture to coordinate long-term irreversible investments with short-term operational adjustments. Five customized methods are designed to solve this model. Numerical experiments are conducted using 30 thousand to 120 thousand batches of cargo data and full-sample carbon emission accounting. Results reveal that as the geopolitical environment deteriorates, total system benefits exhibit a nonlinear accelerated decline. Specifically, indirect affiliated industries prove most sensitive to external risks, whereas core port operational revenue demonstrates strong resilience. The study further confirms that although preventive resilience investments offer limited short-term returns, they effectively curb cost escalation under conflict scenarios. Furthermore, investment in port multimodal transport channels serves not only as a measure for carbon compliance but also as a strategic lifeline to guarantee transshipment continuity amidst geopolitical uncertainty. This paper fills the theoretical gap in foresighted port industry and logistics system planning under geopolitical uncertainty and provides quantifiable graded investment portfolio schemes in practice, offering quantitative decision support for policymakers to seek a dynamic equilibrium among economic benefits, green compliance, and geopolitical security.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Joint dispatching and relocating for dual-service autonomous ride-hailing fleets with rational passenger choice
Authors: Haiyuan Chen, Xinyang Wang, Ruijie Li, Yuanyuan Li, Xiaobo Liu
Abstract: This paper studies the joint dispatching and relocating problem in a dual-service (two-class) autonomous ride-hailing system, where two vehicle types– Express and Premium –serve heterogeneous passengers exhibiting rational but bounded service preferences. Each passenger may exclusively choose one service type or remain indifferent between the two service classes, leading to a state-dependent demand allocation across vehicle fleets. We develop a steady-state fluid model that captures the coupled dynamics among passenger arrivals, service availability, and the platform’s dispatching and rebalancing decisions. The model explicitly characterizes how dispatching probabilities and relocating flows jointly determine the long-run equilibrium of vehicle distribution and system performance. The resulting profit-maximization problem is formulated as a nonlinear program with bilinear terms linking service availability and control variables. By exploiting structural properties of the equilibrium, we show that the nonlinear problem can be reformulated as an equivalent linear program, enabling efficient computation of optimal policies. Using real-world data from the DiDi Tec, we demonstrate the economic and operational implications of the proposed model. Numerical experiments reveal that profit exhibits a non-monotonic relationship with fleet composition–first increasing and then declining as the proportion of Premium vehicles grows–and that service availability saturates faster than profit as fleet size increases. The results provide managerial insights into optimal fleet design and operational coordination for mobility-on-demand platforms.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: RAFT-A: A regime-aware forecast-to-allocation framework for hospital resource planning during outbreaks
Authors: Milton Soto-Ferrari, Amro M. El-Adle, Kuntal Bhattacharyya
Abstract: During epidemic outbreaks, hospitals commit beds, staff, and supplies before demand is realized and while disease dynamics are still shifting. This article introduces RAFT-A, a two-phase framework that connects case forecasting to hospital capacity allocation. Phase I, Regime-Conditioned Forecast Fusion (RCFF), combines five statistical, machine learning, and deep learning models via weighted fusion, whose design is validated through exhaustive evaluation of all model subsets; the ensemble’s diversity yields a predictive distribution of future cases. A regime-detection algorithm classifies epidemic dynamics into growth, plateau, decline, or resurgence. Phase II translates case forecasts into hospitalization demand through a Hospitalization Demand Model (HDM) with validation-optimized weights and allocates resources via Priority-Based Capacity Activation (PBCA), provisioning capacity at the cost-optimal quantile of the predicted demand distribution. The sequential allocation rule is optimal under the cost hierarchy, and the provisioning level follows the distribution-free newsvendor critical fractile, replacing exogenous safety buffers with forecast-error quantiles. We validate RAFT-A using COVID-19 data from Canada, France, Israel, Italy, and the United States spanning April 2021 to May 2022. RCFF and the HDM achieve Mean Absolute Scaled Errors (MASE) below 1.0 (case forecasts: 0.06–0.55; hospitalizations: 0.04–0.55) and predictive distributions with lower weighted interval scores than their seasonal-naïve baselines across all countries and the observed regimes; PBCA maintains zero shortage periods. A decision surface analysis across configurations identifies critical capacity thresholds and quantifies cost–preparedness trade-offs. RAFT-A thus offers hospitals a pathway from epidemic signal to costed capacity decision.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: An empirical study on the adoption drivers of port-shipping blockchain-enabled electronic delivery order platform
Authors: Yige Zhang, Yutong Cai, Haibo Kuang, Fangping Yu, Jianzhao Li
Abstract: In the era of digitalization and the low-carbon transformation of global shipping, the traditional paper-based delivery-order process in container imports remains inefficient, opaque, and prone to security risks. Yet most prior studies have remained largely conceptual, emphasizing the technical features of blockchain while providing limited systematic empirical evidence on the adoption of blockchain-enabled electronic delivery-order (e-DO) platforms in the maritime sector. To address this gap, this study integrates the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), the Technology-Organization-Environment (TOE) framework, and the Diffusion of Innovation (DOI) theory, and further incorporates a multi-stakeholder collaboration dimension to construct a comprehensive analytical framework. Using this framework, we identify 15 key drivers of e-DO platform adoption. Drawing on semi-structured interviews and quantitative evaluations from 38 experts in Singapore’s port and shipping supply chain sector, we employ the Decision-Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory (DEMATEL) approach to uncover the direct and indirect influences among these drivers and to derive their causal linkages and net effects. The empirical findings highlight that document-transfer security, willingness for multi-stakeholder collaboration, data-sharing privacy and access control, and managerial support are the core drivers of platform adoption, with the collaboration dimension emerging as the most critical enabler for accelerating platform diffusion.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Coordinated truck routing and multi-rendezvous drone resupply under shipment release dates
Authors: Thi Hue Tran, Phuong Khanh Nguyen, Huynh Thi Thanh Binh, Huy Hung Tran, Su Nguyen
Abstract: Efficient coordination between trucks and drones is a critical challenge in modern logistics and distribution systems, especially when delayed order availability threatens to disrupt planned delivery routes. In these dynamic settings, drones can be deployed as agile resupply assets to replenish trucks en route, thereby preserving route continuity and boosting overall fleet efficiency. Existing routing models typically restrict each drone flight to a single truck rendezvous, which limits synchronization opportunities and constrains potential improvements in system performance. This paper addresses this limitation by proposing a coordinated framework in which a single drone flight can sequentially resupply multiple trucks. The objective is to jointly optimize truck routes and drone schedules to minimize total system completion time while enabling tighter coordination between ground and aerial resources. To solve this problem, we develop an integrated planning approach that simultaneously manages vehicle routing and drone synchronization decisions. Computational experiments demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms conventional single-rendezvous resupply strategies and obtains high-quality solutions with substantially reduced computational times. Extensive testing across various operational scenarios further confirms the robustness of this approach and its practical relevance for logistics organizations managing complex truck and drone delivery operations.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: A fairness-based scheduling synchronization of lifeboat and powerboat in urban flood emergency rescue
Authors: Yaozong Wang, Yiying Du, Zhihua Hu, Zhongzhen Yang
Abstract: The combined use of lifeboats and powerboats (i.e., buffer platform) is an efficient measure for urban emergency rescue. Lifeboats transfer affected persons from inundated sites to a safe and stable powerboat, after which the powerboat delivers them to the shelter for final evacuation. This study addresses a cooperative scheduling problem that aims to exploit the complementary strengths of these two types of rescue resources. The problem is formulated as an integer linear programming model for lifeboat and powerboat synchronized scheduling. Deprivation cost is integrated into the objective function to capture accumulated humanitarian suffering caused by waiting. Rescue fairness is improved by balancing the waiting burden across disaster sites. Considering the multi-trip and handover operations of the problem, a genetic algorithm and a re-optimization procedure with shaking actions are developed. In addition, a simulated annealing algorithm and a Lagrangian relaxation heuristic are constructed for benchmarking. A case study based on the “7·20” catastrophic rainstorm flood in Zhengzhou demonstrates that the synchronized scheduling can significantly improve both evacuation efficiency and rescue fairness. The results indicate that incorporating deprivation cost enables adaptive adjustments to lifeboat loading and return frequency to the powerboat according to rescue urgency and humanitarian suffering. By balancing the waiting burden across disaster sites, the proposed approach improves rescue fairness while maintaining evacuation efficiency. Compared with increasing lifeboat deployment, reducing the number of lifeboats has a much stronger adverse effect on deprivation cost than on evacuation time, indicating that insufficient resources primarily deteriorate rescue fairness. In addition, a larger affected population further reduces emergency response efficiency and increases waiting burden. Nonetheless, optimizing the stationary point of the powerboat can partially mitigate these negative effects and improve both rescue efficiency and fairness.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: UAV-based urban logistics service network design under demand and weather-induced supply uncertainty
Authors: Zhijia Tan, Qinpeng Wang, Hai Yang, Wei Liu, Zhichun Li
Abstract: Urban low-altitude logistics delivery has increasingly gained public acceptance because it effectively addresses traffic congestion and last-mile delivery inefficiencies. This paper explores the planning challenges associated with urban low-altitude logistics delivery using unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) under demand uncertainty and weather-induced supply uncertainty. Delivery demand naturally varies over time and space, while weather-induced supply uncertainty for UAVs arises from adverse weather conditions. We address this issue by formulating a mixed-integer stochastic programming model, aiming to optimize the allocation of delivery tasks to UAV depots and service intensity to maximize payoff compared to land-based transportation. Supply uncertainty is incorporated by introducing a random parameter to the nominal (planned) supply intensity. By leveraging certain analytical properties of the optimal solutions, the proposed model is simplified to a traditional 0–1 programming problem, which can be solved more efficiently. A case study involving blood delivery using UAVs in Wuhan, China, is presented to demonstrate the proposed model and analysis.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Closed-loop supply chain model with third-party logistics-based return management system
Authors: Sangjun Yoon, Younsoo Lee, Youngchul Shin
Abstract: The rapid growth of e-commerce has led to a significant increase in return volumes, highlighting the importance of the closed-loop supply chains (CLSCs). Handling returned items has become a critical challenge, as companies face uncertainty in return quantities, product conditions, and fluctuating demand in secondary markets. In this study, we develop a two-stage stochastic programming model for CLSCs that incorporates a third-party return management system (3PL-RMS). The 3PL-RMS handles returned items through multiple recovery options, including reuse, secondary-market resale, remanufacturing by suppliers, and disposal. The model captures the complexity introduced by reverse flows and integrates uncertainties related to both returns and secondary-market demand. To solve the model efficiently, we employ the sample average approximation method and a STabilization and Root-cut based Benders Decomposition (STaR-BD) algorithm. Computational experiments show that STaR-BD reduces computation time by approximately 85% compared with traditional Benders decomposition while maintaining solution quality. A case study using realistic e-commerce data shows that integrating a third-party return management system reduces total costs by up to 32% compared with a conventional supply chain model, with savings increasing at higher return rates.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Optimizing urban parcel deliveries: Containerized consolidation on public transport
Authors: Cécile Dupouy, Mellila Kechir, François Clautiaux, Olivier Labarthe, Walid Klibi
Abstract: The integration of urban freight deliveries in public transportation has been identified as a promising strategy for improving middle-mile parcel delivery. In the context of Hyperconnected City Logistics, the problem addressed in this paper is delineated as the coordinated management of parcel flows across multiple logistics service providers, operating within a multi-line, multi-modal public transit network. While the principle of containerization is central to efficient handling, consolidation, and transfer of parcels, its role has not yet been formally conceptualized in the literature. This paper proposes a multi-graph representation and a multi-commodity flow mixed-integer linear programming model to jointly optimize parcel containerization, consolidation, and container routing within the public transport network. Computational complexity is managed through graph reduction techniques that preserve the feasibility space, complemented by a Parcel Shortest Path (PSP) heuristic that restricts parcel routing to shortest paths and an Adaptive Kernel Search heuristic that delivers high-quality solutions within short computation times. To further improve scalability on large instances, we propose a matheuristic approach that uses heuristic solutions to guide the exact optimization process. A case study in Bordeaux, France, demonstrates the efficacy of this approach, with container capacity utilization reaching 70%. This suggests that the approach has the potential to facilitate the efficient integration of freight flows into transit operations, reduce reliance on dedicated freight vehicles, alleviate congestion, and reduce emissions, while maintaining passenger service levels.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Strategy selection of competitive ports and the information value of digital twin in the construction of green shipping corridors
Authors: Shangsong Long, Hui Zhao, Yadong Wang, Lingxiao Wu
Abstract: With the promotion of decarbonization initiatives, many ports are building green shipping corridors (GSCs), which involve the adoption of clean energy and the development of supporting infrastructure between ports. However, uncertainties in clean energy supply costs pose challenges for strategic decision-making. In response, digital twin (DT) technologies, increasingly emphasized in port planning and management, help address these uncertainties by enhancing the availability and quality of information for decision-making. This study considers the information value of DT in GSCs construction, and uses game theory to analyze the strategy selection of two competitive ports in construction of GSCs. We find, first, when the traditional energy adoption ratio is small and in a certain interval, the port with GSCs obtains benefits and gives its opponent without GSCs an interesting free-rider effect thus forming a win–win outcome. Therefore, the practices that both ports conduct GSCs and only one port conducts GSCs can form two interesting win–win outcomes. Besides, when the traditional energy adoption is very small, i.e., below a certain threshold, the port with GSCs has huge competition advantages, thus only one port conducting GSCs will yield a win-lose outcome. Second, under perfect information with DT, many of the win–win outcomes observed under imperfect information are replaced by win-lose results. This suggests that access to accurate clean energy cost information diminishes the free-rider effect of the opponent without GSCs. Third, counter-intuitively, when the market size is large, DT may be over-invested if both two ports adopt DT, and information asymmetry may be better. These findings offer practical implications for port managers considering GSCs construction strategies under conditions of competition and information asymmetry.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Enhancing or damaging? The dual roles of trade credit in shaping supply chain resilience
Authors: Na A, Deyong Yang, Qianchao Wang, Liukai Wang
Abstract: Enhancing supply chain resilience (SCR) has become a critical priority for firms, yet its financial determinants remain insufficiently understood. Drawing on recursive moral hazard theory and cash flow theory, this study examines how trade credit shapes SCR using a large-scale firm-level panel dataset. The results indicate a robust inverted U-shaped relationship between trade credit and SCR. Moderate levels of trade credit enhance SCR by supporting stability and coordination. In contrast, excessive trade credit damages SCR by amplifying liquidity constraints and contagion risks. Further analysis reveals that this nonlinear effect is primarily driven by the response stage of SCR, indicating that firms’ disruption response capacity is particularly sensitive to financial conditions. Moreover, we show that supply chain structure diversity and financial slack mitigate the negative effects of excessive trade credit, highlighting the importance of both network configuration and internal liquidity in buffering risks. These findings provide new insights into the financial determinants of SCR and suggest that trade credit should be actively managed within an optimal range. Managers can use threshold-based approaches to monitor trade credit exposure and adjust financial policies in line with supply chain structure and liquidity conditions to enhance SCR under uncertainty.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Integrated optimization of berth allocation and vessel scheduling under double-berth mooring mode
Authors: Jiao Mo, Hongtao Hu, Xiao Yang, Zhuo Sun, Youcheng Xi
Abstract: The integrated optimization of port seaside resources, including berths and navigation channels, is a pivotal management strategy for enhancing operational performance and mitigating congestion at seaports. Innovative operational modes offer a promising avenue for such optimization. This study introduces the double-berth mooring (DBM) mode, which enables two vessels to moor in parallel at the same berth and be served simultaneously by quay cranes, thereby boosting resource utilization. The integrated optimization is particularly critical in ports with a one-way navigation channel, where vessels are compelled to queue and alternate movements due to unidirectional transit constraints, and where efficient modes like DBM can yield significant benefits. To address this integrated planning challenge, a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model is formulated for simultaneous berth allocation and vessel scheduling, aiming to minimize total vessel dwell time. Given the problem’s complexity, a tailored adaptive large neighborhood search (ALNS) algorithm is developed. It incorporates a three-phase initial-solution strategy based on vessel workflows, a two-layer encoding scheme, and adaptive destroy-repair operators. Numerical experiments demonstrate the algorithm’s efficiency and solution quality, while sensitivity analyses on key operational parameters (i.e., planning time-step, DBM mode, safe navigation distance, operation preparation time, and vessel arrival density) offer valuable managerial insights.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Determinants of investment risk: A comparative analysis of China’s port and manufacturing investments along the maritime silk road
Authors: Dongxu Chen, Yawen Jin, Feng Lian, Fuyu Lai, Zhongzhen Yang
Abstract: Under rising geopolitical tensions, trade conflicts, policy uncertainty, and host-country risks, global logistics systems increasingly require diversified and resilient corridors to maintain trade continuity and transportation efficiency. In this context, China’s port and manufacturing investments along the Maritime Silk Road (MSR) may support corridor resilience by improving logistics node capacity, maritime connectivity, industrial support, and cargo-generation potential. However, investment failure risk may constrain this expected resilience-enhancing role by affecting logistics capacity, industrial support, and corridor diversification. To address these challenges, this study develops a risk analysis framework for port and manufacturing investments along the MSR, incorporating the dimensions of socioeconomic condition, bilateral relations, institutional distance, and sector-specific risk. A binary logit model is used to assess their associations with investment returns, while historical data are used to estimate the probability of investment failure. The results show that: (1) the risk attributes of the port and manufacturing investments differ substantially, i.e., for ports the risk is more closely associated with capital amount, whereas for manufacturing it shows a stronger association with macroeconomic indicators such as Gross Domestic Product (GDP), economic growth rate, openness, and railway network scale; (2) regarding bilateral relations, high-level reciprocal visits demonstrate a long-term cumulative effect, with a four-year lag being more pronounced than a two-year lag; (3) interactions between institutional distance and indicators such as capital amount and logistics performance are significantly associated with variations in risk levels. These results provide evidence-based insights for identifying key risk drivers and for supporting more resilient decision-making on port and manufacturing investments under uncertain geopolitical and trade environments.

Title: Optimizing urban electric vehicle charging and battery swapping infrastructure: A location-inventory-grid model
Authors: Wenqing Ai, Hanyu Cheng, Wei Qi
Abstract: The rapid rise of electric vehicles (EVs) places unprecedented stress on both urban mobility systems and low-voltage power grids. Designing battery swapping and charging networks that are cost-efficient, grid-compatible, and sustainable is therefore a pressing yet complex challenge: service providers must jointly optimize station locations, battery inventory, and grid interaction under high-dimensional uncertainty. We develop an integrated location-inventory-grid model and employ a continuous approximation approach to overcome the intractability of discrete formulations. Our analysis compares centralized versus decentralized charging, with and without participation in frequency regulation. The results reveal that centralized charging, when combined with frequency regulation, not only reduces cost but also strengthens grid stability. However, it may constrain operational flexibility near the optimum, potentially challenging efforts to mitigate environmental impacts by lowering battery inventories. These results offer actionable guidance for cost-efficient, environmentally sustainable, and grid-compatible scaling of urban EV infrastructure to meet the demands of large-scale EV adoption.

Title: Internet of things in rural agricultural freight transportation. A case study of North Dakota State
Authors: Solomon Boadu, Emmanuel Anu Thompson, Ranjit Godavarthy, Evans Akoto, Kwabena Dadson, Herman Benjamin Atuobi
Abstract: Efficient movement of agricultural goods remains critical to economic stability and food supply chain resilience in rural areas. However, traditional logistics systems in rural regions such as North Dakota face persistent challenges such as lack of real-time visibility, flexibility, and responsiveness. These lead to delays, increased costs, and post-harvest losses. Though, Internet of Things (IoT) offers transformative opportunities to enhance these agricultural freight systems, its integration into existing systems remains uneven and underexplored. This study conducts a comprehensive literature review of 60 peer-reviewed articles selected from an initial pool of 730 records to evaluate IoT applications, maturity levels, and implementation barriers in rural freight systems. The findings reveal substantial disparities in connectivity, data integration, sustainability alignment, and policy readiness, particularly in under-digitized rural environments. To address these gaps, the study proposes a six-layer IoT adoption framework tailored to rural agricultural freight transportation. This framework integrates technological, organizational, and policy dimensions to support scalable and context-sensitive implementation. This paper concludes by outlining measurable performance indicators and strategic priorities for policymakers and industry stakeholders seeking to advance resilient and sustainable IoT-enabled rural logistics systems.

Title: Navigating uncertainty in maritime decarbonization: a multi-risk framework for fuel–technology decisions
Authors: Guanqiong Ye, Siqi Li, Han Zhang, Chunyu Lin, Lizhong Yang, Yuling Gao
Abstract: Maritime transport faces growing pressure to align with global net-zero targets, yet investment and operational decisions remain constrained by uncertainty surrounding alternative fuels and decarbonization technologies. Most existing assessments rely on static assumptions and do not capture how transition risks change in different scenarios or interact across political, economic, and technical dimensions. This study develops a multi-risk framework that evaluates six alternative fuels and a broad suite of energy-saving technologies by combining the Entropy Weight Method with Monte Carlo simulation. The framework not only generates risk indices and ranges but also projects the shifting profiles under multiple regulatory and market scenarios from 2025 to 2050. The results show that dominant risk drivers shift over time. Economic factors strongly influence near-term choices, while political and regulatory uncertainties become increasingly important as net-zero regulations tighten. The analysis also identifies a two-stage pattern in technology risks, where early risks are shaped by maturity constraints and later risks are shaped mainly by cost competitiveness. These varying risks create distinct trade-offs between affordability, risk exposure, and well-to-wake emission reduction. From the perspective of the individual performance of fuels and technologies, biofuels and operational measures support lower risk transitions in the short term, while green hydrogen and onboard carbon capture system may become attractive in stricter future policy environments because of their high emission-reduction potential. The study also develops a scenario-based combination evaluation framework to identify the optimal combined fuel-technology pathways under different decision supports for cost, risk, and emission reduction. The framework provides actionable evidence for shipowners, investors, and regulators seeking resilient pathways toward net-zero maritime transport.

Title: Data-driven optimization of a mixed fleet of drones and human couriers for on-demand delivery under uncertainty
Authors: Ziliang Jin, Suhan Wang, Jing Chen, Lingxiao Wu, Ziming Wang
Abstract: On-demand delivery, which allows consumers to receive purchases quickly after ordering, is becoming increasingly prevalent. While human couriers are commonly used for deliveries, they often lead to higher costs and longer delivery times. Drones can help overcome these limitations but have a shorter range compared to human couriers. Therefore, utilizing a mixed fleet of drones and human couriers offers an effective solution for fast, cost-efficient, and reliable on-demand delivery. This paper focuses on an on-demand delivery system in which a mixed fleet of drones and human couriers collects parcels from a central hub and delivers them to parcel lockers across multiple regions throughout a day, under uncertain parcel demand. We propose a two-stage Wasserstein distributionally robust optimization (DRO) model to jointly optimize the allocation and operation of drones and human couriers in the face of demand uncertainty. We propose reformulation techniques to transform the model into a tractable form. To enhance computational efficiency, we develop an L-shaped algorithm and an alternating direction algorithm. Out-of-sample results based on real-world data highlight the benefits of employing DRO approach. Additionally, we reveal that a mixed fleet outperforms using only drones or only human couriers, with drones prioritized for deliveries and serving as the dominant role, while human couriers play a supplementary role. We also examine how the performance of drones and human couriers varies with changes in several key system parameters.

Title: Hybrid quantum AI in logistics and operations management: Operational fit and strategic value
Authors: Markus Bertl
Abstract: Logistics optimization and operations management increasingly depend on artificial intelligence and quantum computing to address complex, time-sensitive planning problems. Existing research has focused mainly on algorithmic benchmarks or speculative quantum advantage, while offering limited insight into how Hybrid Quantum AI creates organizational value under current hardware constraints. This study advances theory by integrating Information Processing Theory (IPT) with the Dynamic Capabilities View (DCV), demonstrating how Hybrid Quantum AI architectures generate organizational value despite the current absence of quantum advantage. Using a case analysis of Malaysia Airlines Cargo (MAB Kargo), it is shown how combining AI-driven data structuring with quantum-enhanced optimization can close critical information-processing gaps and support the development of sensing, seizing, and transforming capabilities. Empirically, this hybrid system achieved an 83% reduction in planning time and a 5% increase in capacity utilization. These findings demonstrate that the current value of quantum computing in logistics lies not in outperforming classical solvers, but in enabling modular, future-ready architectures that improve operational fit today and build strategic agility over time. The study contributes to management and information systems research by explaining “quantum readiness” as an organizational capability enabled by modular digital infrastructure, offering practical guidance for digitization roadmaps and computational investment decisions in next-generation logistics.

Title: Beyond the next port: A multi-task transformer for forecasting future voyage segment durations
Authors: Nairui Liu, Fang He, Xindi Tang, Yineng Wang
Abstract: Accurate forecasts of segment-level sailing durations are fundamental to enhancing maritime schedule reliability and optimizing long-term port operations. However, conventional estimated time of arrival (ETA) models are primarily designed for the immediate next port of call and rely heavily on real-time automatic identification system (AIS) data, which is inherently unavailable for future voyage segments. To address this gap, the study reformulates future-port ETA prediction as a segment-level time-series forecasting problem. We develop a transformer-based architecture that integrates historical sailing durations, destination port congestion proxies, and static vessel descriptors. The proposed framework employs a causally masked attention mechanism to capture long-range temporal dependencies and a multi-task learning head to jointly predict segment sailing durations and port congestion states, leveraging shared latent signals to mitigate high uncertainty. Evaluation on a real-world global dataset from 2021 demonstrates the proposed model consistently outperforms a comprehensive suite of competitive baselines. The results show relative reductions of 4.70% in mean absolute error (MAE), 4.95% in mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) and 2.59% in root mean squared error (RMSE) compared with sequential deep learning models. The relative reductions compared with gradient boosting machines are 7.03% in MAE, 39.49% in MAPE and 4.37% in RMSE. The case study conducted on one major destination port further illustrates the model’s superior accuracy.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: FedGNN-SFCP: Federated graph neural networks for ship fuel consumption prediction with heterogeneous data fusion and missing data imputation
Authors: He Lu, Xing Pan, Wei Yang Bryan Lim, Ran Yan
Abstract: Machine learning (ML)-based ship fuel consumption prediction (SFCP) methods have attracted considerable attention from scholars in recent years due to their robust feature extraction capabilities. However, these methods highly depend on the quantity and quality of ship fuel consumption data. In practice, individual ships generate at most 365 noon reports per year, and privacy concerns prevent data sharing across companies, leading to data scarcity. Additionally, noon reports suffer from coarse daily granularity and missing values, compromising data quality. When ML-based SFCP models are trained on datasets with poor data quantity and quality, their performance degrades dramatically. To address these issues, we propose a novel federated learning (FL)-based method combining graph neural networks (GNN) and generative adversarial networks (GAN) for SFCP, named FedGNN-SFCP. First, to enhance data quality, we propose a GAN-based imputation method for handling missing data in ship noon reports and automatic identification system (AIS) data. Meanwhile, to address the low data granularity of noon reports, we leverage high-frequency AIS data, which provides hundreds of records per day. Specifically, we propose a novel multiple-layer heterogeneous graph construction method and employ a heterogeneous graph transformer to effectively fuse these heterogeneous data sources, thereby improving prediction performance. Second, to enhance data quantity, we introduce FL to SFCP tasks to enable collaborative training, allowing the model to learn from more data while preserving privacy. Furthermore, we propose adaptive federated proximal to address the challenge of training on heterogeneous data feature distributions from different ships. To evaluate FedGNN-SFCP, we conduct a series of experiments on three real-world ship fuel consumption datasets. The proposed FedGNN-SFCP achieves relative reductions of at least 7.21%, 9.63%, and 4.15% in root mean square error, mean absolute error, and mean absolute percentage error, respectively, compared to baseline methods. This demonstrates the effectiveness and robustness of FedGNN-SFCP as a privacy-preserving solution under different data missing rates for SFCP in the maritime industry.

Title: A deviation-based demand-responsive bus service adjustment strategy for same-platform transfers with autonomous rail rapid transit
Authors: Yinfei Feng, Yong Yin, Bisheng He, Bo Du
Abstract: In recent years, the Autonomous Rail Rapid Transit (ART) system, which operates on “virtual tracks”, has been adopted in many cities considering its higher flexibility and lower operating and maintenance cost compared to the traditional metro system. However, a persistent challenge lies in the missing coordination between the ART services and the conventional bus services, frequently resulting in excessively long transfer distance and waiting time for passengers. To address this issue, this study proposes a deviation-based demand-responsive bus service adjustment strategy to facilitate transfers between the bus and ART systems. Under this strategy, when transfer requests are triggered by passengers via devices installed on buses or ART platforms, a bus adjusts its route to enter the ART station platform, thereby enabling same-platform transfers. The proposed mechanism synchronizes bus arrival and departure times with ART schedules to avoid disruptions to ART operations. Furthermore, buses execute these deviations without skipping any scheduled stops to minimize adverse impacts on non-transferring passengers. To further enhance operational efficiency and realism, conditional stop control and holding control strategies are incorporated, along with time-varying traffic conditions. A mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) model is formulated to jointly minimize both passengers’ and operators’ time. The model is decomposed into two subproblems, and solved using a hybrid Gurobi − Adaptive Large Neighborhood Search (GALNS) algorithm. The proposed model and algorithm are validated through a real-world case study in Yibin, China. Promising numerical results indicate that, by adopting the proposed deviation-based demand-responsive strategy, the total time decreases by 1.12%, 0.42%, 21.75%, and 23.48%, respectively, compared to solutions without considering demand responsiveness, control strategies, route deviation, and any strategy. The proposed bus service adjustment strategy provides a valuable guidance on improving the flexibility of conventional bus operations and enhancing the convenience of transfers between the bus and ART systems.

Title: The impact of ESG performance on trade credit: the role of operations and supply chain management factors
Authors: Lujie Chen, Fangxu Yan, Fu Jia, Yonggui Wang, Chenho Chao
Abstract: Environmental, social, and governance (ESG) practices have increasingly garnered attention on a global scale, highlighting the importance of understanding the potential consequences of ESG performance. The objective of this study is to examine the impact of a firm’s ESG performance on the behaviors of suppliers, with a particular emphasis on the trade credit provided by these suppliers. Furthermore, this research also analyzes operations and supply chain management (OSCM) factors such as operational efficiency (OE), supplier concentration (SC), and R&D intensity (R&D), which may serve to moderate this relationship. To achieve these goals, we perform a secondary data analysis encompassing 2,046 listed companies in Chinese manufacturing industries from 2018 to 2023 and find that the performance of corporations in terms of ESG displays an inverted U-shaped correlation with trade credit. Moreover, OE and R&D intensity steepen the inverted U-shape and shift the turning point to the left, while SC flattens the inverted U-shape and also shifts the turning point to the left. These findings suggest that ESG has important logistics and supply chain consequences because it shapes suppliers’ willingness to provide the short-term financing that helps stabilize procurement, production, and delivery activities. In light of these findings, we provide a noteworthy contribution to the existing literature on buyer–supplier relationships and logistics fulfilment presenting important implications for both researchers and practitioners in the domain of OSCM.

Title: Learning-based emergency egress trajectory planning for UAV in mixed terminal airspace
Authors: Lichen Su, Shulu Chen, Yuhao Wang, Leyan Chen, Zhiheng Li, Kai Wang, Xiaobo Qu
Abstract: Advanced air mobility (AAM) is expected to introduce increasingly heterogeneous low-altitude operations, and mature AAM deployment may create locally high-density traffic around capacity-constrained vertiports. This paper considers mixed operational scenarios in which unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) aircraft share the same vertiport and surrounding terminal airspace. In such environments, eVTOL operations typically follow air traffic management (ATM) procedures and are strategically deconflicted in advance, resulting in schedules that are largely inflexible. By contrast, certain UAV missions, such as time-critical medical deliveries following intercity eVTOL transport, require immediate departure and cannot wait for global replanning. Safely allowing emergency UAVs to egress from locally dense or capacity-constrained terminal airspace without disrupting pre-planned eVTOL operations therefore poses significant operational challenges. To address this problem, we develop an Asynchronous Proximal Policy Optimization (APPO) based reinforcement learning approach for emergency UAV egress that explicitly encodes separation safety and egress efficiency. A distributed policy-training framework based on Ray RLlib is developed, and the simulation environment incorporates the AirLib flight-control model from AirSim to represent low-level UAV maneuver responses during speed and heading command execution. Simulation results demonstrate that, under locally dense terminal traffic conditions, the proposed approach demonstrates stronger overall robustness than APF, VO, RRT, Modified CL-RRT, and MCTS-UCT in terms of safe-egress performance, separation maintenance, and online computational efficiency.

Title: Customer digital-intelligent transformation and suppliers’ new quality productivity: evidence from supply chain spillovers
Authors: Jiazhan Gao, Guihong Hua, Lu Yang, Baofeng Huo
Abstract: Digital and intelligent technologies are beginning to alter the way major customers interact with upstream suppliers. Beyond improving customers’ own operations, these technologies may also change how demand information, transaction data, and innovation resources move across vertical supply chains. This paper examines this possibility by studying whether customer digital-intelligent transformation (CDIT) is associated with suppliers’ New Quality Productivity (NQP), defined as a structural upgrading of production capability that goes beyond conventional input–output efficiency and innovation-output efficiency. Based on supplier–customer matched data for Chinese A-share listed firms from 2009 to 2022, the evidence shows a positive relationship between customers’ digital upgrading and the productivity quality of upstream suppliers. The finding remains stable after using alternative measures, addressing endogeneity, correcting sample-selection bias, and changing empirical specifications. Mechanism analysis indicates that CDIT contributes to supplier upgrading by improving supply–demand alignment, easing financing and transaction frictions, and strengthening digital-intelligent innovation collaboration. The effect is stronger among large suppliers, state-owned suppliers, and firms more dependent on major customers. Overall, the study develops a customer-driven vertical productivity reconfiguration framework, showing how digitally transformed customers reorganize information, transaction, capital, and knowledge flows across customer–supplier relationships and convert firm-level digital capabilities into suppliers’ NQP.

Title: Data-driven UAV network design for emergency medical services under spatio-temporal uncertainty
Authors: Haoyan Li, Zhongqi Wu, Shaoxuan Liu
Abstract: Designing reliable Unmanned Aerial Vehicle networks for Emergency Medical Services is fundamentally challenged by the profound multi-dimensional uncertainty of demand. Existing approaches typically rely on static coverage or steady-state queueing models with fixed average arrival rates, often failing to capture the complex interplay between intra-day fluctuations, inter-day stochasticity, and dynamic spatial shifts. To address this, we propose a novel data-driven two-stage distributionally robust optimization framework under Wasserstein ambiguity sets. Unlike traditional methods, we model the demand arrival rate profile itself as a random variable, thereby endogenously characterizing how temporal volatility induces spatial uncertainty. We formulate the problem by integrating facility location and capacity dimensioning with a queueing system to ensure response reliability. To tackle the resulting computational intractability caused by nonlinear critical traffic intensity constraints, we derive an exact linearization and reformulate the problem into a mixed-integer linear program. We further develop an Accelerated Mixed-integer Benders Decomposition algorithm, enhanced by valid inequalities via Sample Average Approximation, robust warm starts, and Reformulation-Linearization Technique cuts. Extensive numerical experiments using real-world data demonstrate that our proposed algorithm reduces computational time by orders of magnitude compared to standard decomposition methods. Furthermore, out-of-sample analyses reveal that our model significantly outperforms traditional queueing-based benchmarks, effectively mitigating tail risks and ensuring operational resilience in data-sparse and data-rich regimes alike.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Rail-to-city emergency supply operations for protective accessibility: Evidence from conflict-affected Kharkiv
Authors: Andrii Galkin, Serhii Lyfenko, Denis Lomotko
Abstract: Urban logistics in high-intensity emergencies, where armed conflict represents an extreme case, faces disruption that threatens timely and equitable access to essential goods. Conventional supply chain models optimise cost and efficiency, yet crisis response must also protect recipients by limiting exposure during access trips. This study develops a rail-to-city decision-support model that integrates rail backbone corridors with alternative last-mile channels under security constraints and operationalises protective accessibility as a threshold service standard (within 15 min vs over 15 min). Using Kharkiv (Ukraine) as a case, we construct a city-scale digital network (street topology, geocoded service points, and demand zones) and evaluate six feasible configurations combining alternative sets of rail stations (adaptive micro-hubs) with last-mile channels (volunteer couriers, postal/CEP service points, pickup points, and lockers). For each configuration, we estimate transport work (pk·km), route distance and time, the population share within the 15-minute threshold, and equity indicators for vulnerable groups. Results show that activating additional rail gateways yields an approximately linear reduction in total delivery distance (∼35,000 km per added station) and substantially expands ≤ 15-minute coverage; a hybrid rail–postal configuration improves protective coverage by up to 40 % relative to volunteer-only delivery. The findings provide implementable guidance on gateway activation, service-point densification, and actor-burden allocation to improve protective accessibility and resilience in protracted urban emergencies.

Title: Two-echelon robot-assisted electric vehicle routing problem with pickup stations
Authors: Nima Moradi, Fereshteh Mafakheri, Chun Wang
Abstract: Parcel distribution is the costliest, most time-consuming, and most emissions-sensitive leg of e-commerce’s last-mile logistics. We study a multimodal system that pairs robot-assisted delivery with self-pickup. The problem is motivated by an emerging integrated planning architecture in dense urban and campus settings, where Electric Vehicles (EVs) replenish local service points, while the last mile is completed by sidewalk robots and Pickup Stations (PSs). We formalize this setting as the Two-Echelon Robot-Assisted EV Routing Problem with PSs and Service Designations (2E-REVRP-PSSD). We propose a compact Mixed-Integer Linear Programming model and a two-stage matheuristic, coupled with a size-aware Simulated Annealing Adaptive Neighborhood Search and a two-index EV routing optimizer. Across small- to large-scale benchmarks, the matheuristic delivers strong solution quality, robustness, and scalability: it matches best-known solutions on small instances in seconds; on medium- and large-scale instances, it outperforms a two-hour Gurobi run on average and returns feasible plans for all cases within minutes. We also applied our proposed method to related benchmark instances and obtained 9 new best-known solutions, which are reported in the literature. Sensitivity and scenario analyses yield actionable guidance: depot-biased or demand-centered siting reduces first-echelon miles; discrete thresholds in capacity/range and pickup-station coverage unlock stepwise consolidations; EV choices dominate CO 2 reductions; and Pareto frontiers expose inexpensive gains in battery-risk margins but steep costs for extreme pickup convenience. The framework is directly applicable to dense urban neighborhoods, campus districts, and retailer-locker networks where EVs feed robot hubs and pickup stations, enabling low-carbon, customer-aware last-mile logistics.

Title: Solving a rich vehicle routing problem with a heterogeneous fleet and trailers in medium-sized transport companies
Authors: Robin Aninger, Stefan Voigt
Abstract: Efficient route planning is a critical challenge for transport companies operating heterogeneous vehicle fleets. Manual planning often fails to leverage cost-saving consolidation opportunities, leading to suboptimal capacity utilization and increased operational costs. This paper addresses a real-world vehicle routing problem involving pickup and delivery tasks, heterogeneous vehicles and trailers, time windows, service equipment requirements, and labor constraints. We develop a matheuristic method that combines heuristic tour construction with exact optimization using a set partitioning model leveraging the manageable number of stops per tour.The proposed matheuristic is validated using real operational data from a medium-sized logistics provider based in Germany. Our experiments demonstrate that the matheuristic achieves average cost savings of 16.6% compared to historical plans, with solution times well under three minutes even for large instances. A comparison with a pure optimization model shows that while exact methods can yield marginally better solutions (up to 2–3% improvement), they are computationally impractical for real-time use. The matheuristic strikes a practical balance between solution quality and runtime, enabling automated, scalable, and cost-efficient routing for medium-sized transport companies with a heterogeneous fleet.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Interactive Bi-LSTM: A novel approach for multi-channel vessel traffic flow prediction
Authors: Yang Chen, Zhao Liu, Mingyang Zhang, Xinyu Wang, Xiuju Fu
Abstract: Accurate prediction of vessel traffic flow (VTF) is essential for enhancing maritime safety and improving the efficiency of cargo transportation and port operations. In multi-channel waterways, VTF exhibits strong temporal variability, pronounced fluctuations, and complex inter-channel correlations, which pose significant challenges for reliable forecasting. Existing deep learning methods often fail to effectively capture the dynamic interaction effects among channels, as well as the coupled spatiotemporal dependencies inherent in VTF data, leading to suboptimal prediction accuracy and stability. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a Multi-Objective Interactive Deep Learning Network (MOIDLNet) based on the Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) architecture. The proposed model introduces a novel hidden-state interaction mechanism that enables dynamic information exchange across channels within a unified temporal modeling framework, thereby effectively capturing inter-channel dependencies and their evolving patterns. In addition, a hybrid loss function, termed MSEDTW, is developed by integrating Mean Squared Error (MSE) with Dynamic Time Warping (DTW), allowing the model to jointly optimize point-wise accuracy and global temporal consistency. Extensive experiments are conducted on real-world AIS datasets collected from the Chengshan Jiao Promontory (CJP) and Caofeidian Port (CFDP). Sensitivity analyses on key hyperparameters, including iteration number, learning rate, and input sequence length, are performed to determine optimal model configurations. The experimental results demonstrate that MOIDLNet consistently outperforms conventional machine learning methods and representative deep learning models in terms of prediction accuracy and stability. These findings highlight the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed approach and its potential for supporting intelligent maritime traffic management.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Adaptive air traffic management via large language model augmented reinforcement learning
Authors: Shulu Chen, Amin Tabrizian, Peng Wei, Yuhao Wang, Xiaobo Qu
Abstract: Urban Air Mobility (UAM) presents a transformative approach to urban transportation by enabling safe and rapid air travel. However, ensuring safety remains a critical prerequisite for large-scale deployment. Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) has demonstrated promise as a tactical deconfliction method, offering real-time speed advisories to maintain safe separation between aircraft.
